The Digital Twin serves as a virtual representation of patients, simu lating their
responses to various treatment actions. This environment allows for testing PRIME-
Care without direct clinical involvement, providing insights into the potential outcomes
under various clinical scenarios.
properties.source_ref: Papers/088_2025_PRIME-Care A Unified Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Optimization Framework for Personalized Treatment Planning Under Clinical Uncertaint.pdf

properties.content:
The PRIME-Care experiments relied on two complementary data sourc es. The ﬁrst
dataset consisted of longitudinal, de-identiﬁed electronic health r ecords (EHR) from a
regional multicenter chronic-care program, comprising approximately 19,000 patient
trajectories with irregular time sampling and heterogeneous covariat es. The dataset
included demographic attributes, laboratory results, clinician-re corded disease severity
indices, administered interventions, and adverse-event marker s. Because PRIME-Care
explicitly models uncertainty propagation, the irregularity and incompleteness
of the trajectories provided a realistic testbed for evaluating th e eﬀectiveness of the
framework’s probabilistic state estimators, which were designed to handle missingness
without information leakage.
The second data source consisted of high-ﬁdelity digital-twin simul ation environ-
ments parameterized by the real clinical data distribution. These simulators were
developed using physiologically meaningful nonlinear dynamics relate d to chronic dis-
ease progression and were validated through expert-driven calibration p rocedures.
properties.source_ref: Papers/088_2025_PRIME-Care A Unified Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Optimization Framework for Personalized Treatment Planning Under Clinical Uncertaint.pdf

properties.content:
All experiments were conducted under a sequential decision-maki ng setting in
which PRIME-Care determined individualized intervention seq uences such as med-
ication titration, scheduling of diagnostic assessments, and lifesty le adjustment
recommendations. A clinical advisory board oversaw the mapping betwe en algorithm
outputs and clinically feasible actions, ensuring that the simulati on does not include
unrealistic therapeutic choices.
properties.source_ref: Papers/088_2025_PRIME-Care A Unified Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Optimization Framework for Personalized Treatment Planning Under Clinical Uncertaint.pdf

properties.content:
Each baseline was executed using identical patient histories, cov ariate representa-
tions, and digital-twin dynamics. Hyperparameters and training sched ules were tuned
through systematic cross-validation to prevent confounding performan ce diﬀerences
due to suboptimal conﬁgurations. This comparative setup allowed for an un biased
assessment of the hybrid RL optimization structure in PRIME-Care, isolating con-
tributions from constraint feasibility modeling, belief-state un certainty handling, and
the bilevel decision structure.
6.3 Evaluation Metrics
The evaluation protocol was designed to assess four principal dimension s of algorithmic
and clinical performance: patient safety, personalization ﬁdelity, p redictive accuracy,
and robustness under perturbation. Safety was quantiﬁed through the f requency of
constraint violations involving medically deﬁned thresholds for adve rse biomarkers or
treatment toxicity. Personalization quality was assessed via traje ctory similarity analy-
sis, measuring the alignment between algorithm-generated plans and ex pert-annotated
individualized strategies. Predictive accuracy was evaluated usin g the negative log-
likelihood of state-transition predictions and the concordance inde x for longitudinal
progression forecasting.
Robustness was measured by evaluating the stability of treatment dec isions under
perturbations to model parameters, missingness patterns, and stoc hastic noise within
the digital twin. PRIME-Care’s probabilistic formulation permitte d uncertainty-aware
variants of these metrics, enabling direct comparisons with uncert ainty-agnostic RL
baselines. All metrics were reported with conﬁdence intervals de rived from 5,000
bootstrap resamples to ensure statistical reliability.

For datasets without explicit explanation ground truth, TAXAI constructs reference alignment signals using 
one of the following proxy strategies:
• Clinical priors: anatomically plausible regions (e.g., lung fields in chest imaging) extracted via standard seg-
mentation templates.
• Perturbation-based pseudo-ground truth: regions whose occlusion produces the largest prediction drop.
• Concept-level references:  ranked clinical features (e.g., perimeter_worst, concavity) derived from estab -
lished diagnostic literature in tabular datasets.

and held-out test sets, respectively. The validation set was used for model tuning and early stopping, while final

cross-validation (KFold, n_splits = 5) was applied exclusively within the training portion to assess robustness, 
and fold-wise Trust Index values were averaged. Final performance metrics were computed on the independent 
30% test set.

translation, zoom, and horizontal flipping. A standard hold-out split (70% training, 30% validation) was applied.

properties.content:
A convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier was implemented with three convolutional blocks:
• Conv2D filters: 32 → 64 → 128
• MaxPooling after each block
• BatchNormalization for training stability
• Dense layer (256 units) with Dropout (0.5)
• Softmax output layer for multiclass classification
Training was performed using Adam optimization with categorical cross-entropy loss over 22 epochs and batch 
size 32.
properties.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf

properties.content:
Tabular benchmarks were evaluated using LightGBM classifiers trained on structured diagnostic features. Class 
imbalance was addressed using ADASYN oversampling prior to model fitting. Detailed dataset characteristics, 
including class distribution, acquisition context, and stratified data splitting protocols, are provided in the 
Supplementary Information (Table S6) to ensure transparency of the experimental setup.
Cross-validation and hyperparameters
Performance was estimated using fivefold cross-validation. Key hyperparameters included:
• Gradient boosting with 50 leaves
• Learning rate = 0.1
• Feature fraction = 0.8
• Maximum depth = 12

properties.rationale: The documented input list contains property and transaction attributes, without a separated intervention/command input. Covariate editing would not automatically supply action semantics.

properties.applicability_reason: No explicit or latent action variable requires mapping to executable operations.
The executed experiment delivers no physical or clinical intervention. Consequences of a future financial service are outside this scope, not presumed reversible or harmless.
No intervention or command input requires parameters, timing or units. Regression weights are not action attributes.
No intervention sequence is modeled. Transaction year and predictive-draw count are not action timing.
No action regimes are queried. Sparse transaction coverage is predictive input support, not intervention positivity.
No modeled action space exists to classify by role or effect channel.
The actual experiment is non-agentic offline analysis, not an authorized system proposing or executing environmental actions. Proposed financial use is not demonstrated automation.
No operational agent tool-call boundary is defined. Keras use and map attribution are not inference-time agent calls.
Two comparator regressors are not interacting decision agents; no agent coordination is defined.
No proposal-making agent exists to revise actions through feedback. Parameter fitting is not reflection.

properties.rationale: The specified computational paths are feed-forward regressors and statistical analysis, not LLMs or decision-making agents.

properties.applicability_reason: No intervention-effect identification argument exists requiring estimand-linked assumptions. Weight priors and ordinal encodings are different modeling assumptions.
Price outputs are not presented as identified intervention effects. Anticipated improvement from screening is an untested benefit proposal, not validated causal assurance.

properties.rationale: The defined target is factual static price prediction, without intervention alternatives or a causal contrast. ANN–BNN comparison is not an intervention estimand.

properties.applicability_reason: Observed prices reference factual regression, not alternative intervention outcomes. Predictive draws are not potential outcomes under distinct actions.
No causal estimand is targeted. Bayesian parameter inference is not causal identification.
No action-to-state physical or pharmacological mechanism is modeled. Expert advice for categorical preprocessing is not mechanistic intervention semantics.
No causal effect or identification assumption is assessed. Possible prior/convergence explanations are not confounding-sensitivity analyses.

properties.rationale: Missing/invalid-value counts, masks and placeholder treatment are not reported; complete inputs are not assumed.
Collection and decision-time information availability are not distinguished. Future-information leakage is not demonstrated.

properties.applicability_reason: No temporal resampling grid or timing-dependent event/history target is defined. No EndoClock regime is assigned.

properties.rationale: No site-local retention or federated artifact-exchange protocol is reported. Distributed Bayesian references are not implementation evidence.

properties.applicability_reason: No trajectory or elapsed-time transition is modeled. Sales spanning multiple years do not create an irregular-time forecasting task.

properties.rationale: A random reserved holdout is stated. Training-only preprocessing, property-identity separation and architecture-selection/test separation are not established. Neither leakage nor its absence is demonstrated.

properties.applicability_reason: The assessed static regressors do not carry asynchronous measurements through sequential updates. Property age is not elapsed time since measurement.

properties.rationale: The animal example and data link identify provenance context, but do not establish variable-level source, units, timestamps, transformations and version retention in the proposed framework.
Spike timing is important in the review, but retention or reversible recovery of native observation times at a declared processing resolution is not documented for the proposal.
Acquisition time is not distinguished from processed-signal availability, and no training or query procedure enforcing information-release times is reported.
No measured/missing/invalid indicator is specified. An interval with no spikes must not be interpreted as missing recording or valid silence without an explicit validity convention.
No per-variable freshness representation or carry-forward update rule is provided. The unresolved acquisition design does not establish either use or inapplicability.
Discussion of spike timing and neural dynamics does not supply a proposal-specific prediction rule using actual unequal observation intervals.
Retinal stimulus-response encoding is discussed, but no framework-specific model represents when, whether or why observations become available conditional on acquisition context.
No target/grid-specific witness-preservation test is reported. Biological timing importance does not establish an observation-clock audit or permit a clock-regime assignment.
No target measurement schema or traceable unit/terminology conversions are specified. Correspondences between biological circuits and neural-network motifs are not data harmonization.
No original split, stimulus/recording overlap audit, preprocessing-fit boundary or availability audit is supplied. A public data link establishes neither leakage control nor leakage.
No site-local data retention, exchanged artifacts or federated training/query protocol is described.
Encoding is explicitly reviewed and recommended. Adapted CNN examples do not establish an operational encoder belonging to the future integrated framework, as required by this implementation feature.
No named pretrained checkpoint and adaptation procedure is specified. Transferring computational ideas from cortex to retina is not checkpoint reuse.
No implemented context-to-target-representation loss is specified for the proposal. Biological spikes, hidden variables and an autoencoder bottleneck alone do not meet this criterion.
No qualifying predictive-representation objective or anti-collapse mechanism is supplied. WTA competition and biological inhibition are not demonstrated anti-collapse controls for such an objective.
Reconstruction is central to the review and prior decoder. Its executed loss is not established for the new integrated proposal; details and earlier results remain attributed to [76], not inherited.
Combining computational approaches is not a specified fusion operation over two input modalities. Serial stimulus-to-spike-to-image mappings do not establish multimodal fusion.
No fusion rule conditioned on modality availability, quality or recency, or defined missing-modality behavior, is reported.
Recurrent motifs and HMMs are reviewed, but no implemented carried state/history is defined for the integrated proposal. This does not deny states in the cited methods.
The probabilistic-coding discussion supplies no proposal-specific posterior/filter over hidden state conditioned on observation history.
Encoding and decoding are not separate prior propagation and observation correction operations. No missing-observation correction semantics are specified.
An adjustable device is envisaged, but updating a maintained individual state from arriving measurements during sequential use is not reported.
The precision-medicine motivation is not a patient-specific parameter or weight-adaptation rule. Fitting receptive fields in cited work is not adaptation by the proposal.
Multiple applications and computational examples are discussed, but the same maintained state/checkpoint feeding at least two typed tasks is not established.
No original ablation tests omitted state/history against specified targets. Adapted receptive-field comparisons are not sufficiency tests of the integrated proposal.
Spike-history filters and recurrent networks belong to reviewed approaches; an operational history-conditioning mechanism is not assigned to the integrated proposal.
No matched history-swap, withholding or population-prior control tests individual predictive value. Personalized-device aspirations and animal decoding do not establish it.
No transition-level identity/anatomy memory, constraint or consistency loss is specified. Qualitative reconstruction similarity is insufficient.
Biological explanations and adapted filter visualizations do not define an inspectable maintained state of the proposal. Gap-junction function remains an explicit uncertainty.
Recurrent motifs motivate future work, but no executed memory/read mechanism or context window is specified for the integrated framework.
Stimulation is an envisaged operation, but no settable command is shown to condition a relevant prediction. Presented visual inputs are not automatically therapeutic-action queries.
The narrative distinguishes visual input, neural responses and stimulation, but supplies no operational action vocabulary with role/effect-channel typing.
Electrode targeting, stimulation parameters, units, timing and duration sufficient for an interpretable or executable query are not specified.
No stimulation start/stop times, command cadence or duration semantics are given. Spike-recording time is not an intervention schedule.
No joint stimulation-command or replacement/partial-update/inheritance semantics are defined. Multiple electrodes alone would not establish coherent bundle handling.
Operational stimulation bounds, contraindications and candidate restrictions are unreported. Reconstruction fidelity is not a hard action constraint.
Retinal stimulation is recognizable conceptually, but no calibrated mapping from an operational action representation or desired spike pattern to executable commands is established.
No context-conditioned coverage, overlap or mechanistic-support criterion is estimated and tested for candidate stimulation alternatives.
No reported experiment compares predicted successors under two specified stimulation alternatives from the same initial context. Comparing reconstruction methods is not L3 action comparison.
Physical reversibility, residual effects and harm after stopping stimulation are not assessed for the proposal.

No implemented carried-world-state transition or successor coordinate is defined for the proposal. Movie reconstruction and inference evolution do not establish future-state dynamics; cited recurrent methods are not inherited.
Learned encoding and reconstruction in prior studies do not establish a learned/identified transition over a declared health-world coordinate in the proposed framework.
No successor-state model consuming a settable stimulation action is specified and evaluated. Possible decoder-based control does not establish L2 prediction.
Poisson spikes, neural sampling and probabilistic inference are reviewed, not specified as a conditional next-world-state process of the integrated proposal.

Anatomy and circuit motifs motivate structural design, but their executed constraint on learning/inference in the proposal is not established. Biological analogy alone fails the operational criterion.
Hybrid motifs are future work; no operational mechanistic–learned coupling with fixed/fitted/learned quantities specified is established. The word hybrid is insufficient.
Surveying several modeling approaches is not interchangeable dynamics under shared state/action/time/output semantics; no exchange or integration test is reported.
Cells, synapses and circuits are discussed, but no explicit cross-scale state/constraint exchange is implemented. Retinal layers and CNN hierarchies alone do not qualify.
No training objective traverses two predicted world transitions. Joint training of decoder stages is not multi-step dynamics training.
No options, variable-duration events or coordinated timescales define transitions of the proposal. Layered visual processing does not establish temporal abstraction.
Decoder relevance is explicit, but execution of an observation-emission mapping from the integrated proposal's maintained state is not established. The illustrated decoder is prior work [76].
No implemented state-to-clinical-outcome head with target, units and horizon is supplied. A reconstructed stimulus is not automatically a reward/value or patient-benefit head.
No original successor-state prediction experiment evaluates the proposed framework. Reconstructing the same presented video and reviewing neural-response studies do not establish L1.
No two successive transitions consume generated state/history. Multiple reconstructed video frames do not establish recursive future rollout.
No sequential forecasting evaluation defines intermediate ground-truth feedback. Recorded spikes used for reconstruction are not evidence of teacher forcing across world transitions.
No predict/act, newly measure, correct-state and forecast-again sequence is executed. The authors' encoding/decoding loop does not establish measured re-assimilation.
No maximum evaluated future-prediction extent is stated. Biological milliseconds and the one-second raster scale are not forecast horizons.
No common-protocol error/violation comparison across free-running forecast depths is reported. Generalization limitations are not measured rollout drift.
No horizon curve, acceptance tolerance, uncertainty and action-support context justify a usable forecasting limit.
Reviewed neural sampling does not establish conditional future trajectories or a joint forecast distribution for the proposal.
No request interface or policy rejects, transparently truncates or escalates unsupported horizons. An actual unsafe acceptance behavior is not inferred.
A possible decoder-based stimulation-assessment signal is proposed; simulated future consequences feeding ranking, search or policy learning are not implemented.
No operational WM-coupled optimizer/policy and control results are reported. WTA circuitry or cited constraint-satisfaction work does not establish L4.
No plan-prefix execution followed by measured-feedback replanning is specified, and planning/execution horizons are unreported.
Separate encoding/decoding stages do not establish a fixed learned transition supporting changed utilities or constraints without retraining.
No uncertainty-dependent candidate scores, constraints or acceptance rule is supplied. Probabilistic neural computation does not itself establish risk-sensitive planning.
No optimized plan is tested under independent/mismatched dynamics or adversarial support/reward conditions. No exploitation failure is inferred from this reporting gap.
No candidate stimulation-set construction, eligibility, support or coverage definition is reported. Stimulus images are not a documented candidate-action set.
Multilayer networks and circuit motifs do not establish higher-level options/goals governing lower-level stimulation actions with duration and termination semantics.
No evaluation shows this framework's actions changing an environment and measured responses driving subsequent decisions. Reconstruction and the authors' terminology are insufficient.
Probability coding and sampling are reviewed, but no original predictive uncertainty distribution/set with defined target semantics belongs to the proposed framework.
Neural variability is not an estimated separation of aleatoric and epistemic prediction uncertainty; no such procedure is reported.
No predicted probabilities/intervals/sets are compared with frequencies or coverage using a defined target, metric and validation sample.
No joint-path or horizon-indexed reliability protocol is supplied. Reconstructed video and recording time do not establish forecast-trajectory calibration.
No calibration acceptance tolerance or result against it is reported. Neither successful calibration nor a failed test can be assigned.
Generalization limitations and denoising examples do not specify an operational OOD statistic, threshold, protective response or detection result.
No nonconformity score, calibration split and coverage/error-control assumptions define conformal prediction or alarms.
No stimulation alternatives, population, outcome horizon and causal contrast define an estimand. General graphical-model causal language does not supply one.
No estimand-linked identification argument or assignment/data design is supplied. A Bayesian network's directed graph does not itself establish identified stimulation effects.
No identification assumptions are tied to a stimulation-effect estimand. Biological motif hypotheses and assumptions in cited encoding models are not such an assumption set.
No analysis quantifies violations of confounding, selection, model or support assumptions for a proposed intervention effect.
The illustrated animal reconstruction is not validation of predicted stimulation effects against known potential outcomes or controlled interventional responses.
Anatomical motivation does not provide a calibrated action-to-retinal-state mechanism with identified parameters and applicability. Gap-junction function is explicitly unresolved.
Estimand, justified identification/mechanism, support, validation and sensitivity do not collectively establish a causal-effect assurance claim. This is not a failed causal experiment.
No implemented blocker, stimulation-limit enforcement or fail behavior is reported. Computational scope and conceptual status do not make future physical safeguards irrelevant.
No trigger withholds an action/recommendation and enters a defined fallback or review route. Neural sampling is not abstention.
No escalation trigger, available human role, response timing or fallback semantics are defined for the future framework.
Possible reconstruction-based feedback does not define a runtime hazard detector with triggers and protective response.
No tested stop, safe degradation or fallback protocol and residual-effect assessment is reported.
No assets, adversary capabilities or attack paths across sensory inputs, neural representations, decoding and stimulation interfaces are analyzed.
No attacks/faults are injected into the integrated proposal. Adapted image-denoising illustrations are not an adversarial or safety-fault evaluation of it.
No operational privacy mechanism is specified. Public animal data do not establish privacy controls or their inapplicability to a future human sensory device.
No copying, membership, re-identification or attribute-disclosure test is reported. Intended stimulus reconstruction is neither a memorization audit nor itself a privacy failure.
No authentication, allowed actors or enforced actuator-operation scope is specified. Envisaged stimulation does not establish actual device integration or permissions.
No interface/protocol for appropriate reliance, uncertainty communication or override is specified or evaluated. Scientific caveats are not operational trust mitigation.

properties.applicability_reason: The static prognosis component maintains no evolving hidden health-world state over an observation history. Bayesian parameter and outcome uncertainty are not a filtering belief over such a state.

properties.rationale: No fitting rule updates an individual's parameters or weights using new personal measurements. Group partial pooling and patient-specific features do not establish adaptation; an explicit fixed-parameter deployment configuration is also absent from the reporting.

properties.applicability_reason: The static predictor does not propagate or generate patient/anatomical/scene identities across transitions. Cross-transition identity preservation has no operation to constrain; patient indexing and data identity remain separate concerns.

properties.rationale: No matched correct-individual versus swapped/withheld/population-prior control is reported. Patient-level prediction and global modality removal do not establish personalization evidence.

properties.rationale: The proposed CDSS includes source attribution, audit logging and version logging, and the research agenda discusses provenance. These do not specify measurement-level retention of source, units, acquisition/availability times, transformations and dataset identity. No operational provenance-preserving input adapter is reported for this composition.

Figure 4 proposes medical-image, structured-EHR and free-text inputs without specifying retention or reversible availability of native event/acquisition timestamps. Literature-search dates and Table 6 roadmap years are not observation timestamps. The unspecified temporal input contract prevents either a positive retention assertion or an assertion that timestamps are discarded.

The proposed retrieval and clinical-input workflow does not distinguish specimen/acquisition time from result-release or information-availability time, or specify availability-respecting training queries. Current guideline retrieval and clinician verification are different responsibilities. Availability semantics remain relevant to the proposed EHR-based advice, rather than being inapplicable.

The conceptual multimodal input/fusion path does not specify measured, missing or invalid indicators supplied to the model, placeholder semantics, or missing-modality processing. Out-of-scope abstention is a proposed output safeguard, not an observation-validity mask. No incompatible imputation mechanism establishing absence is reported.

Although structured EHR inputs include laboratories and vital signs, the proposed architecture does not specify carry-forward behavior, asynchronous updates, or variable-level time since true observation. Guideline currency and post-deployment monitoring do not establish measurement freshness representation.

No prediction rule in the proposed composition uses actual unequal elapsed intervals, native event timing or continuous clinical-time integration. The feedback/correction loop is a workflow proposal, and roadmap years are implementation-planning horizons. Neither establishes irregular-time prediction; no explicit uniform-spacing assumption establishes absence.

The diagram identifies observation modalities but supplies no model or rule for when, whether or why measurements occur conditional on patient or acquisition context. Retrieval grounding and clinician corrections are not a measurement-generation process. The article does not document an operational model explicitly treating sampling as ignorable either.

Figure 4's audit trail concerns versions, drift and performance surveillance. No target distinction and sampling grid, or witness-preservation test involving values, update/validity patterns, native timing and external channels, is reported. A generic audit box does not establish an observation-clock audit, and missing reporting is not evidence that a completed preprocessing audit omitted one.

Multimodal fusion and cross-site infrastructure are proposed, but source-specific clinical terminology, units and measurement definitions are not mapped to a declared target schema with traceable conversions. Feature fusion alone is not semantic/unit harmonization. No documented invalid mapping or incompatible concatenation supports an absence assertion.

For the proposed CDSS, no development cohort, train/test partition, preprocessing-fit boundary or audit of decision-time feature availability is specified. Recommendations for external validation do not establish leakage control. Literature deduplication belongs to the review methodology, not patient-level predictive-data leakage prevention. This does not contradict G01 being inapplicable to the review's own non-predictive contribution.

Sections 8.3 and Table 6 recommend federated, privacy-preserving multicentre infrastructure. The review supplies no own protocol defining participating sites, local-data retention, exchanged artifacts or federated training/query operations. The recommendation is not an implemented federation, and cited federated systems are not inherited. No explicitly central-pooling implementation establishes absence.

Figure 4 explicitly proposes modality encoders and fusion upstream of the model core. However, the paper does not define an operational observation-to-feature mapping, encoder architecture, output representation or executed path for this composition. The diagram establishes a recommended responsibility, already captured by conceptual relations, but does not meet this feature's operational evidence criteria. It is not evidence that encoders are absent.

The review discusses foundation models and future multimodal pretraining, but selects no named encoder checkpoint/version and describes no transfer or adaptation within its proposed composition. Names of surveyed models and the generic RAG-grounded model-core box do not establish foundation-encoder reuse. Training from scratch is not established either.

No context-to-target representation prediction loss is specified for the proposed CDSS. Discussion of latent diffusion, general representation learning or CLIP-style image–text pretraining does not establish a predictive-latent objective in this composition. There is no complete own training objective from which either presence or absence of a latent-target term can be established.

The proposed model has no reported predictive-representation objective, anti-collapse constraint or representation-collapse test. GAN mode collapse discussed in the literature review is a different phenomenon and supplies no evidence for this feature. Because the proposed core's training mechanism is unspecified, the parent dependency is unresolved rather than explicitly excluded; not_applicable and absent are not justified.

Reconstruction, denoising and generative imaging appear as applications of surveyed model families, not as losses of the proposed Figure 4 composition. No own loss compares reconstructed observations with observed targets. Secondary image-quality ranges do not establish such an objective, and no complete objective explicitly excluding reconstruction supports an absence assertion.

criteria_met: Figure 4 separately identifies medical images, structured EHR and free-text inputs.
The proposed workflow routes these inputs through a common modality-encoding and fusion stage.
criteria_missing: The fusion operator and modality-interaction mechanism are not specified beyond the high-level workflow.
Scope-matched execution or results establishing operational multimodal fusion are not reported.
properties.rationale: The partial assessment is limited to the proposed architecture: identifiable modalities and an intended shared fusion stage are documented. It does not establish implemented fusion, fusion effectiveness or the capabilities of cited multimodal systems.

The proposed fusion stage does not specify availability masks, modality-quality or recency conditioning, or behavior when an input modality is missing. General multimodal recommendations do not establish availability-aware fusion, and no requirement for complete modalities is documented that would establish absence.

Figure 4 specifies information flow and clinician feedback but does not define an explicit or latent patient state, or an event history carried into a subsequent prediction/update. Retrieval storage, audit logs and a feedback arrow alone do not establish persistent evolving-state semantics.

Uncertainty/calibration guardrails and recommended uncertainty methods do not define a posterior or filtering distribution over a hidden individual state. Neither a belief-state model nor an explicitly deterministic point-state alternative is reported for this composition.

Clinician corrections are mentioned, but no prior-state propagation, observation-conditioned posterior correction, or missing-observation update rule is defined. Human review of recommendations is not evidence of a propagate–correct state estimator.

The feedback/correction loop does not specify updates to a current individual state when new measurements arrive. It could concern model corrections, retrieved content or workflow documentation; no sequential patient-state assimilation procedure or result resolves that ambiguity.

No individual parameterization, patient-specific fitting objective, measurement-driven adaptation rule or weight-update protocol is supplied. The proposed clinician feedback cannot establish patient-specific parameter adaptation, and the paper does not explicitly fix all parameters population-wide.

The review discusses multiple imaging and CDSS tasks but does not define one propagated state/checkpoint feeding at least two typed readouts. A common model-core box and broad application coverage do not establish shared-state reuse or separately trained task-specific alternatives.

No ablation or probe evaluates omitted history, variables or state representations against a prediction/decision target for the proposed composition. The nine-dimensional literature appraisal is not a state-sufficiency test, and cited systems' experiments are not transferred to this design.

EHR inputs and retrieval are proposed, but no mechanism identifies a patient's prior observation/action sequence and explains how it conditions a current inferred state or forecast. Patient-specific recommendation language does not establish longitudinal history conditioning.

No matched history-swap, history-withholding, population-prior or analogous comparison tests individual-specific predictive value for this composition. Recommendations for integrated evaluation and clinician–AI team testing do not constitute a personalization audit.

The review discusses anatomical hallucination risks, but its proposed composition specifies no memory, constraint or loss preserving anatomy, modeled entities or patient identity through transitions. Source attribution and audit logging are not identity-consistency mechanisms.

Explainability, attribution and clinician verification are discussed or recommended, but no carried state's variables or latent coordinates are mapped to inspectable clinical entities or physiology. Qualitative architecture-family explanation ratings do not establish interpretable state semantics for this composition.

No recurrent history state, temporal context window, ordered state–action memory or other mechanism retaining prior observations/actions is specified for the proposed system. The retrieval store and audit trail are not documented as temporal predictive memory; transformer terminology alone is insufficient.

Documented clinical decisions/actions and clinician accept/edit/reject choices are downstream workflow elements, not specified settable intervention inputs conditioning a future-state prediction. Free-text queries are not operationalized as intervention commands. The high-level diagram does not establish either an explicit action-conditioned predictor or a fully documented incompatible mechanism.

The review distinguishes diagnostic measurements, predictive alerts and generative recommendations, but does not supply an action vocabulary separating therapeutic, inquiry/acquisition, procedural, behavioral or operational roles with their effect channels. These output/use distinctions do not meet the typed-action criterion, and an uninterpreted action-vector implementation is not established either.

The proposed CDSS produces recommendations followed by clinician verification and a documented clinical action, but does not define an operational action schema with applicable targets, parameters, units, routes, timing, duration or reference frames. General medication-safety examples do not establish parameterized action queries for this composition.

No intervention start/stop times, administration cadence, duration or dose-schedule representation is specified for the proposed CDSS. Table 6's 0–2, 2–5 and 5+ year intervals are research-roadmap horizons, not patient intervention schedules.

The architecture does not specify joint treatment components, full-replacement versus partial-update semantics, inherited settings or preservation of linked interventions. Reviewing polypharmacy and medication interactions does not establish a coherent treatment-bundle representation in the proposed system.

Figure 4 recommends safety guardrails, out-of-scope abstention and clinician verification, but supplies no context-dependent action bounds, contraindication rules or candidate-filtering algorithm. Those general oversight requirements do not establish the action-constraint mechanism defined by this feature.

The downstream clinical decision/action box does not define encoded action variables or their mapping to specified clinical operations, device commands or executable interfaces. Clinician accept/edit/reject authority is a proposed review boundary, not a demonstrated semantic or executable action mapping.

No context-conditioned regimen coverage, overlap, propensity or mechanistic support criterion is estimated, justified and tested for this composition's recommendations. Retrieval grounding, source attribution and out-of-scope abstention are not themselves evidence of support for alternative clinical actions.

No results apply at least two specified actions to the same initial patient/history and compare predicted successors for the proposed system. The review's architecture-family comparisons and cited clinician-versus-LLM comparisons are different comparison types and cannot establish this feature or L3 capability.

The authors distinguish supervised assistance from high-stakes autonomous use and require clinician verification, but provide no action-specific assessment of physical/clinical reversibility or residual harm after execution. Rejecting a recommendation before use is not an analysis of whether a delivered intervention can be reversed.

The proposed workflow does not define a carried health-world state/history advanced to a successor under elapsed time or a declared transition coordinate. Clinician feedback and audit-monitoring arrows do not establish such a transition. Descriptions of diffusion denoising and language generation in cited model families are not temporal-dynamics evidence for this composition.

No health-world transition training objective, fitted transition parameters, learned transition structure or learned mechanistic correction is reported for the proposed CDSS. A generic LLM/predictive-model core and feedback of clinician corrections do not establish learned dynamics. The review does not supply an original trained model experiment.

No settable intervention/regime input to a health-state transition, intervention-query pathway or action-conditioned successor result is specified. The diagram's clinical decision/action is downstream of clinician review, not an evidenced conditioning input to predictive world dynamics.

No conditional random next-state process or transition sampling procedure is defined for this composition. General discussion of probabilistic generation and a proposed uncertainty/calibration guardrail do not establish stochastic world-state transitions, uncertainty decomposition or calibration.

The proposed architecture supplies no physiological equations, conservation rules, anatomical constraints, monotonicity conditions or symbolic structure constraining a transition or learned representation. Retrieving clinical guidelines is a proposed information-grounding mechanism, not a demonstrated mechanistic inductive constraint.

No mechanistic and learned dynamics components are operationally coupled with identified fixed, fitted and learned quantities. Combining encoders, retrieval, an LLM/predictive core and human review is not sufficient to establish mechanistic–learned hybrid dynamics.

The review compares architecture families and labels a generic LLM/predictive-model core, but documents no two interchangeable dynamics implementations sharing state, action, time and output semantics, and no integration or replacement test. Compliance scoring and low-trust referral are proposed, but context-dependent clinical action bounds, contraindications or workspace restrictions are not specified or tested. The workflow names response delivery and referral to a clinician, but does not define model action variables and their operational mapping to clinical procedures, calibrated device commands or executable interventions. No historical action dataset, context-conditioned overlap estimate, coverage criterion or mechanistic support test for queried alternatives is reported. Neither the narrative healthcare application nor the claimed case-study benefits report predicted successors under two specified actions from the same initial patient, scene or history. Comparing multiple LLM responses or describing delivery versus referral is not a matched alternative-action prediction experiment. Functional L3 evidence is therefore not established.

The paper discusses patient safety, misleading advice and escalation, but reports no assessment of action reversibility or residual harm after a response or recommendation has affected care. criteria_met: The two source resources are identified by name and URL, with reported access dates and source-specific image counts.
The preprocessing recipe documents resizing, border addition, blurring and RMS-based duplicate removal.
criteria_missing: Exact dataset releases and record-level source/transform lineage are not reported.
Retained per-image acquisition and availability metadata are not reported.
Post-deduplication counts and traceable membership of the final partitions are not reported.
properties.rationale: This is partial source-and-transformation traceability for the shared five-model benchmark, not evidence of a complete variable-level provenance service or an evaluated provenance audit.

properties.applicability_reason: The evaluated task classifies independent static photographs and defines no temporal observation stream, acquisition-time resolution or successor coordinate at which native timestamps would be retained. This judgment is limited to the static benchmark and does not imply that photograph timestamps could never matter in another use.

properties.rationale: Pages 5–8 describe capture instructions, image upload, cloud processing and inference, but do not distinguish image acquisition time, upload/receipt time and information-release time or describe availability-aware query construction. Real-time wording and visible chat timestamps do not establish this feature.

The image-preparation methods describe resizing, a black border, blur and deduplication, but no measured/missing/invalid indicators supplied to any of the five classifiers. Image-quality variability remains relevant, so single-modality input alone does not justify inapplicability. The black border is not evidence of a validity mask.

properties.applicability_reason: The evaluated model processes a static photograph without carried-forward variables, asynchronous patient measurements or a longitudinal state. Per-variable freshness updates under carry-forward therefore have no dependency in this configuration. Longitudinal tracking is explicitly future work.

The static classification task contains no time-indexed prediction requests or unequal observation intervals to model. The reported 50 epochs are optimization passes, not clinical sampling intervals or a continuous-time transition.

properties.rationale: Capture tips and user image submission are described, but no model or operational rule represents when, whether or why observations occur conditional on patient state or acquisition context. The acknowledged patient-generated image variability makes acquisition-process questions relevant; guidance alone does not establish an observation-generation model.

properties.applicability_reason: The inspected pipeline performs spatial preprocessing of independent images, not temporal resampling of an event stream onto a grid. No temporal target distinction or sampling grid exists for a clock-witness audit in this configuration. Possible loss of visual pathology through blur or resizing is a different audit question.

properties.rationale: The two resources are pooled under cancer/non-cancer labels and common image dimensions, but source-specific diagnostic definitions, label mappings, image schema/color conventions and traceable semantic conversions are not described. Spatial resizing and blurring do not establish semantic or unit harmonization.

criteria_met: The reported preparation removes image pairs flagged by an RMS-error threshold before describing partitioning of the resulting dataset.
Separate training, validation and test subsets are specified.
criteria_missing: Patient-level and lesion-level independence across partitions is not established.
Source overlap and robustness of duplicate detection to crops or transformations are not audited.
Training-only fitting and validation-only tuning/model-selection controls are not sufficiently documented.
Final partition identifiers, counts and reproducible split controls are not reported.
properties.rationale: Only an image-redundancy and partition-separation subset is documented. A random split alone is insufficient, and neither the split nor RMS filtering proves complete leakage control. No leakage event or successful comprehensive leakage audit is inferred.

The privacy limitations explicitly identify federated learning as not yet implemented, and the conclusion places federation in future work. Absence is scoped to the reported implementation; GDPR-compliance wording does not establish a federated protocol or its privacy effectiveness.

The executed Generic CNN maps preprocessed oral images through convolutional features to binary classification. Table 3 reports 3 × 3 filters and 64 filters, and Table 4 documents classifier execution. This establishes observation encoding, not persistent state or a separately evaluated encoder representation; no isolated encoder test is reported.

DenseNet121 provides an executed image-to-feature mapping within the static classifier. Its reported configuration has 121 layers and growth rate 32. End-to-end classification results do not establish a maintained world state or a standalone representation-quality evaluation.

DenseNet169 operationally extracts image features for binary classification; the reported configuration has 169 layers and growth rate 32. Classification execution supports implementation of the mapping, not temporal encoding or a separately tested representation objective.

The reported 201-layer, growth-rate-32 DenseNet maps oral photographs to classification features. This is implemented observation encoding within a static model; network depth and classifier results do not establish a world-state representation or an isolated encoder evaluation.

InceptionV3 extracts multi-scale image features for the evaluated classifier and is reported as integrated into the chatbot. Implementation of this observation mapping is supported; a persistent state, predictive-latent objective and separately validated encoder representation are not established.
The Generic CNN description and training table provide filter and training settings but no named pretrained checkpoint, transferred representation or explicit from-scratch initialization.
DenseNet121 names an architecture, not a used pretrained checkpoint. Initialization source, checkpoint/version, frozen layers and adaptation of transferred parameters are not specified.

The DenseNet169 implementation is described by architectural depth, growth rate and common training settings. No named pretrained asset or its adaptation is reported; customary pretrained use cannot be assumed.

No pretrained initialization, checkpoint identity or transferred encoder adaptation is specified for DenseNet201. Its architecture citation and longer CPU training do not resolve whether pretrained weights were used.

The selected InceptionV3 classifier has no reported pretrained checkpoint/version, initialization source or adaptation protocol. A cited transfer-learning application does not establish transferred parameters in this system.

The Generic CNN is trained for static image labels. The paper gives only a generic description of loss, not a complete objective or any context-to-target-representation loss. Internal convolutional features do not establish predictive-latent training; the incomplete objective prevents a definitive absence assertion.

No representation-target prediction term is specified for DenseNet121. Dense connections and feature reuse concern architecture, not a latent predictive objective. The reported classification task and unspecified loss do not supply a complete objective permitting a stronger negative conclusion.

Methods describe DenseNet169 classification and common training settings but no target encoder, context/target representation pair or latent prediction loss. Static diagnostic performance cannot establish this training mechanism.

No context-to-latent-target objective is reported for DenseNet201, and the mathematical training loss is not supplied. Its learned image features and network depth are insufficient evidence for predictive-latent training.

InceptionV3 produces static classification scores and CAM visualizations. No latent target, representation prediction term or predictive pretraining procedure is specified. CAM generation is not evidence of such an objective.

No anti-collapse mechanism, representation-variance constraint or collapse test is described for the Generic CNN. Because a complete representation objective is not supplied, neither predictive-objective applicability nor explicit omission/collapse is established.

DenseNet121 feature reuse and stable gradient-flow motivations do not specify representation-collapse prevention. No anti-collapse objective or test is reported, and no collapsed representation should be inferred from low classification performance.

No DenseNet169-specific anti-collapse mechanism or diagnostic is supplied. General claims of convergence and generalization do not establish this feature; the incompletely specified objective also prevents a dependency-based inapplicability judgment.

The paper reports DenseNet201 architectural and training settings but no anti-collapse constraint, guarantee or test. Extended training runtime and weak diagnostic agreement are not evidence for either collapse prevention or observed representation collapse.

Neither the selected classifier's description nor its CAM integration specifies an anti-collapse mechanism or representation-collapse evaluation. Highest reported classification scores do not substitute for this evidence.

properties.rationale: The methods provide more than dataset names: they identify the simulated-image generation pathway and several operational transformation parameters. They do not establish the complete measurement-level provenance contract.

properties.applicability_reason: The scoped predictor maps a static context projection and relative source angle to another view of the same CT anatomy. It has no modeled temporal resolution at which native event or acquisition timestamps must be retained. Angle coordinates are not timestamps.
properties.rationale: This disposition concerns native temporal information for the reported view-prediction task, not a general claim that imaging timestamps lack clinical importance.

properties.rationale: The supplied methods describe image sources and downstream evaluation but do not distinguish image collection, processing and information-release times or specify an availability-time audit. This does not establish that future information entered training or evaluation.

properties.applicability_reason: The reported predictor does not carry asynchronous measured variables forward through patient time. It conditions on one context image and a geometric displacement, so per-variable time since last observation has no operative role in this scoped mechanism.

The transition coordinate is relative source rotation, not irregular clinical observation time. Randomly sampled angles, angular step sizes and sinusoidal token positions do not constitute elapsed-time handling. No longitudinal temporal prediction is included in this scope.

scope.time_horizon: Acquisition angle rather than elapsed time

properties.rationale: This is an implemented synthetic acquisition-observation rule: the anatomy and source configuration determine the generated observation, and angle sampling determines which target views enter training. It is not a model of endogenous clinical ordering, informative missingness or the timing of real examinations.

scope.population: CT-derived projections of fixed chest anatomy

properties.applicability_reason: The scoped task defines neither a temporal event distinction nor temporal resampling of an observation stream. properties.rationale: The rotation-step experiment must not be relabeled an EndoClock audit.

properties.rationale: Common input resolution and representation-domain alignment are described, but source-specific measurement definitions, intensity units or terminology are not mapped through traceable conversions to a declared semantic target schema. No leakage violation is established.

The paper reports dataset-based training on eight GPUs but no site-local data retention, federated rounds or exchanged model artifacts. Multiple datasets and multi-GPU training do not establish federation; the description also does not provide the explicit incompatible source-record pooling evidence required for an absence assertion.

An EMA encoder maps target projections into supervision features.
Input resolution and patch size are operationally specified.
properties.rationale: The encoder pathways are described mathematically and used in the reported training and evaluation pipeline. EMA parameter updates concern optimization, not patient-state assimilation.

Table 1 evaluates the ViT-Base representation on five CXR benchmarks. This is encoder-utility evidence, not an acquisition-transition accuracy result or a clinical acceptance test. Complete splits and an acceptance tolerance are not reported.
Table 1 separately evaluates the ViT-Large representation. Its reported result is not assigned to the ViT-Base model, a specific reconstruction decoder or prospective clinical use.

The supplied methods name ViT architectures and describe X-WIN pretraining but do not identify a transferred initialization checkpoint or explicitly state training from scratch. Reused foundation models in the comparator panel are not components of X-WIN. Additional training details are referred to an unavailable appendix, so neither checkpoint reuse nor its absence is established.

criteria_met: Context-image features and an explicitly embedded source angle produce predicted target-view patch features.
Target features come from the EMA image encoder.
InfoNCE, target-affinity alignment and patch-feature matching supervise prediction in representation space.
properties.rationale: The operational objective predicts another acquisition view's representation, not an evolving disease state. The main masked-token branch also matches target representations rather than establishing a pixel-reconstruction objective.

The paper evaluates the contrastive latent-prediction objective and its combination with masked modeling through downstream classification ablations. This establishes an evaluation of representation-training choices, not direct anatomical truth, clinical causality or a specified prediction-error tolerance. Exact Figure 4 point values are not tabulated.

scope.population: VinDr linear-probing evaluation used for the loss-function ablation

criteria_met: The implemented InfoNCE objective explicitly attracts corresponding predicted-target representations and repels nonmatching representations.
The identity-label InfoNCE term is retained alongside the softer target-affinity regularizer.
properties.rationale: The nonmatching-pair repulsion is an operational anti-trivial-representation mechanism, not merely an algorithm citation. Coding its anti-collapse role is reviewer inference from the specified loss. No dedicated collapse diagnostic, guarantee against collapse or measured collapse-prevention effect is reported. The domain-loss stop-gradient is not treated as separate proof of representation-collapse prevention.

The specified main pretraining objective comprises latent contrastive/affinity alignment, masked target-token representation matching, latent patch/domain alignment and domain classification. Figure 2 supplies target representations through the EMA encoder. None of these terms compares a reconstructed observation image with observed image values. Thus observation-space reconstruction is absent from this explicitly delimited pretraining mechanism. This does not deny the separate projection-decoder experiment.

scope.population: Main X-WIN representation-pretraining objective in Equations (1)–(11), excluding the separately trained VQ-GAN decoder

properties.rationale: For all four decoder configurations, the paper reports training a VQ-GAN decoder with ground-truth projections and evaluates rendered-image PSNR/SSIM. It does not specify the decoder's training-loss terms in the supplied document and defers details to an unavailable appendix. Image generation and fidelity metrics establish reconstruction outputs, but do not by themselves identify an implemented observation-reconstruction loss. A standard VQ-GAN loss is not inherited from the cited architecture.

properties.applicability_reason: The implemented observation pathway encodes two-dimensional radiographic images. CT volumes generate simulated radiographic training targets; no separately encoded CT-voxel representation is fused with a CXR representation. Real and simulated radiographs are training domains, not separately fused observation modalities. The source-angle input is an action, not a second observation modality.
properties.rationale: The documented single-observation-modality pathway makes multimodal observation fusion inapplicable in this scope. CT-derived supervision and multiple datasets do not establish a multimodal fusion operation.

properties.applicability_reason: The scoped encoder does not fuse separately available observation modalities. Consequently there is no multimodal availability, quality or recency-dependent fusion operation to assess.
properties.rationale: Random patch masking for the masked-modeling objective is not conditioning fusion on whether an actual clinical modality was observed. This applicability judgment does not establish general missing-data robustness.

criteria_met: An encoded context projection supplies a defined latent patch state to a subsequent prediction operation.
The view predictor advances that representation to target-view patch representations under a specified source-angle displacement.
The encoder and view predictor are operational components reused in the reported rendering experiment.
properties.rationale: The evidence is not an embedding alone: Equation (1) uses the origin representation in a learned successor-view mapping. This satisfies the supplied carried-state criterion at single-transition scope, without establishing recurrent memory, posterior filtering or recursive rollout.

scope.time_horizon: One direct acquisition-view displacement from the encoded origin; not elapsed clinical time

value.persistence_extent: Origin representation carried into an acquisition-successor prediction

properties.rationale: The specified forward-state mechanism maps encoded context patches and an embedded angle to point-valued target patches. Its operational state has no hidden-state posterior or filtering-distribution interpretation. The contrastive softmax scores compare representation pairs during training; they are not a belief distribution over patient or anatomical state. This negative assertion is limited to the documented latent-view operator, not uninspected repository code or every possible decoder extension.

The described query operator predicts target-view features directly from the encoded origin and action. It contains no observation-conditioned correction operation separate from prediction. The EMA target encoder and target-patch matching provide training supervision, not correction of an inferred state when a new measurement arrives. Absence is therefore scoped to this documented operator rather than inferred merely from missing filtering terminology.

The supplied document describes direct target-angle predictions from a context projection, but no sequential inference protocol that updates a current individual state with arriving measurements. Training-time EMA updates and downstream fine-tuning do not demonstrate observation assimilation. No broader claim that all conceivable sequential uses are impossible is made.

Population pretraining, benchmark-level few-shot fine-tuning and a separately trained projection decoder are described. None supplies a patient-specific parameter-fitting rule using that patient's measurements. Frozen components in particular experiments do not establish a universal absence of individual adaptation in unspecified uses.

Linear probing freezes the vision encoder rather than defining and training a new state encoder for each probe.
criteria_missing: The supplied methods do not establish a single identical state/checkpoint feeding at least two distinct typed tasks beyond separate CXR classification benchmarks.

Classification uses the EMA encoder, whereas the reconstruction experiment names the frozen context encoder and view predictor; these cannot automatically be treated as an identical shared state artifact.
properties.rationale: Reusable representation transfer is demonstrated, but the stronger shared-state, multiple-typed-readout criterion is incompletely established. The reconstruction branch is not merged with the classification branch to manufacture checkpoint identity.

The supplied version does not report removing or withholding state/history components to test whether transition determinants remain represented. Classification linear-probe performance and improved reconstruction are not, by themselves, a state-sufficiency assessment.

Equation (1) conditions on a single supplied context projection and the requested angle. No mechanism incorporating earlier patient/scene observations or prior actions before that origin is described. The sampled target projections supervise training; they are not an observed history supplied to the predictor. Current-snapshot conditioning is retained as such rather than promoted to longitudinal history conditioning.

properties.rationale: The document reports prediction targets from the same CT volume and projection/CT reconstruction fidelity, but no matched subject-input swap, withholding control or population-prior comparison testing the added value of the correct individual's information. properties.rationale: This codes the existence of an implemented loss intended to retain anatomy through a geometric view change, not proof that anatomical or patient identity is always preserved. The specified default operator takes the current encoded context projection and target angle, without additional history memory. Spatial patch attention and positional encoding are not temporal memory, and EMA updates model weights during training rather than retaining an individual's observation history. This scoped absence does not characterize the separately reported step-wise ablation and is not a claim that a Markov-style view predictor is intrinsically defective.

value.default_action: Relative source yaw angle a_i = k·Δϕ

properties.rationale: This separately records evaluated use of the explicit action in the rendering configuration. Aggregate rendering fidelity does not establish per-angle action sensitivity, matched alternative-action comparison, a validated acquisition range or clinical action safety.

properties.rationale: The source explicitly defines the action as radiation-source rotation producing a different projection of the same CT anatomy. properties.rationale: The operation, parameter, unit and relative reference are sufficiently specified to interpret the offline target-view query. properties.rationale: This determination is restricted to the default direct-view predictor. It does not classify the separate step-wise training ablation as an implemented timed acquisition program.

scope.time_horizon: One direct target-view query specified by relative source angle

properties.applicability_reason: The scoped action is a scalar source-angle query, not a treatment regimen containing linked clinical components or inherited treatment settings. Treatment-bundle replacement and partial-update semantics therefore do not apply.
properties.rationale: The yaw-pitch-roll ablation is a geometric parameterization alternative, not evidence of a clinically coherent treatment-bundle mechanism.

The training procedure explicitly restricts candidate source angles. This establishes geometric sampling bounds only, not a runtime rejection mechanism, radiation-safety envelope, clinical contraindication check or empirically validated action-support criterion. The reported angular range and candidate counts are retained without inventing an endpoint convention.

This satisfies semantic grounding within the simulation query. Calibrated commands for an actual scanner, device integration and physical execution are not established by this assertion.
properties.value: Semantic grounding to simulated source yaw in degrees, with corresponding cone-beam projections generated from the same CT anatomy

properties.rationale: The supplied version describes an angular grid, random target sampling, rotation-step ablations and aggregate rendering fidelity. It does not report a context-conditioned coverage, overlap or support criterion evaluated for queried alternatives. Generating physically defined training targets and clipping the sampled angle range do not by themselves establish such a support assessment. This is insufficient reporting, not evidence that all queries are unsupported.

Several target angles can be generated from the same CT/context, but the reported results do not sufficiently identify a comparison of predicted successors under at least two specified alternative actions from a matched origin. Table 3 compares training action designs through downstream classification AUROC; Table 5 reports aggregate rendering/reconstruction fidelity. Standard VQ-GAN mechanisms cannot be inherited from citations. The reported useful representations also do not establish that collapse was observed.

The authors train a VQ-GAN and subsequently freeze it, but no externally pretrained encoder checkpoint or transferred initialization is identified. Training the encoder in the first stage does not establish that initialization was from scratch. CheXFound, DINOv2 and iGPT comparisons are not foundation-encoder reuse by Xray2Xray.

criteria_met: The transition target is a sequence of learned, quantized projection representations produced by the separately trained VQ-GAN encoder.
Equation (2) trains conditional prediction of those next-view representations using token negative log likelihood.

properties.rationale: This satisfies the supplied operational criterion for predicting a target representation, specifically discrete learned latent codes rather than raw pixel tokens. It is not a claim that the method implements JEPA, a continuous embedding-matching loss or reconstruction-free training of the complete system. properties.rationale: This excludes multimodal fusion, not the documented two-view feature aggregation.

properties.rationale: Missing-view handling and image-quality robustness would remain separate reporting questions; they are not established by this applicability judgment.

Scoped design absence: the specified inference algorithm recursively predicts from its own preceding outputs, and the illustrated synthesis explicitly receives no extra information. There is no distinct observation-conditioned correction operation within this executed rollout. This does not assert that a future extension could not add one.

Updating generated token state is not assimilation of newly arriving evidence. The absence assertion concerns this protocol, not an untested general interface capability.

Population pretraining, a frozen vision encoder, frozen downstream features and image-conditioned inference are described. No patient-specific parameter-fitting or weight-update rule using new individual measurements is reported. Frozen components alone are not treated as proof that every possible adaptation mechanism is absent.

Separately trained readouts evaluate CVD risk classification and five-pathology classification.
properties.rationale: This establishes representation reuse, not one unchanged clinical classifier or external validation of a fixed composed system. CheXpert additionally uses CycleGAN input-domain transformation.

Downstream classifiers probe representation utility, and Table 3 compares model depths and conditioning views. No matched omission, alteration or sufficiency-oriented probe isolates which state/history determinants are required for the prediction targets. properties.applicability_reason: Fixed within-scan windows are encoded; no carried-forward asynchronous measurement state is maintained whose freshness must be updated.

properties.rationale: Incomplete assurance is not proof of leakage.

Downstream tasks reuse Brain-JEPA's own pretrained target encoder. This phase is distinct from initial pretraining. The paper pins the configuration, not a unique checkpoint hash.
A latent-target objective is operational and compared through downstream evaluations. This does not establish strict future-only forecasting or universal superiority over reconstruction.

The asymmetric predictor and moving-average target branch are a specified anti-collapse design mechanism. This is a mechanism-level interpretation of the documented computation, not an inherited guarantee from I-JEPA. Stop-gradient details, dedicated collapse tests, and a non-collapse proof are not reported.
The proposed objective explicitly avoids masked-input reconstruction. Reconstruction in BrainLM/MAE comparators is not assigned to Brain-JEPA.

properties.applicability_reason: The implemented encoder uses fMRI alone. ROI subdivisions and multiple cohorts are not different modalities; MEG/EEG/T1 integration is future work.

properties.rationale: Patch embeddings and target prediction are explicit, but persistence of a health-world state into a subsequent transition/update is not. No posterior/filtering distribution or hidden-state uncertainty semantics are specified. Masks and EMA do not supply them.
Distinct prior propagation and measured-observation correction operations are not specified. The target encoder is not a filtering correction.
No sequential updating of an individual's existing state from arriving measurements is reported. Re-encoding and parameter training are different operations.
Task/cohort fine-tuning is described, not per-patient fitting using that patient's new measurements.

A common pretrained representation feeds separate age, sex, and amyloid probes. This restricted representation-level reuse does not establish a persistent state, identical fine-tuned task weights, or one jointly deployed state service.

The operational criterion includes representation-information ablations: 3 versus 30 gradient components are tested against specified readouts. This records a narrow assessment, not proof of sufficient state, Markov sufficiency, transition determinants, or a passed clinical tolerance.

Subject-specific temporal context is used, but no current-state or forecast origin defines which observations are prior history. Supplied image notes describe targets on both temporal sides. A causal-prefix or sequential-state protocol would resolve the stronger feature.
No matched history-swap, withholding, or population-prior control is reported. Cross-cohort performance and representation ablations answer different questions.
