The binary lesion-region channel is an anatomical ROI mask, and the causal Transformer mask restricts attention. Neither establishes measured/missing/invalid status for observations. Handling of missing visits, unavailable clinical covariates, or invalid measurements is insufficiently reported.

Observed-prefix restrictions and temporal attention masking are described, but acquisition time is not distinguished from the time MRI-derived measurements, masks, or clinical variables became usable. No release-latency audit is reported. This reporting gap does not establish use of prematurely available information.

No target-specific temporal witness-preservation audit is reported across sampled values, update/validity patterns, native timestamps, or external acquisition channels. MRI phase selection and voxel cropping are not such an audit. No observation-clock regime is assigned.

Public de-identified multicenter trial resources are described, but no site-local training/query protocol or exchanged federated artifacts are reported. Multicenter data and de-identification do not establish federation. The source does not meet the explicit negative criterion involving centrally pooled identifiable records.

Adaptive phase selection, eight-channel construction, robust intensity normalization, and standardized voxel-array dimensions are described. These preprocessing steps do not sufficiently document source-specific units, terminology, and measurement definitions mapped to a declared semantic target schema with traceable conversions. Successful cross-cohort prediction does not establish that contract.

The executed transition uses learned visit-position embeddings. Actual elapsed intervals, native event times, and continuous-time integration affecting predictions are not reported. The source also does not explicitly establish the absent criterion of assuming uniform spacing while ignoring known unequal intervals. Neither irregular-time handling nor uniform clinical cadence is inferred.

criteria_met: The source-fold models, pCR readouts, and operating thresholds are reported as fitted using I-SPY2 only.
External probabilities are averaged across source-fold models, and the mean source-validation threshold is transferred without target-outcome fitting or selection.
criteria_missing: A formal participant-overlap audit between the trial resources is not reported.
Complete source-only fitting and transfer details for every preprocessing and response-target construction statistic are not explicitly audited.
Information-release timing and relevant site/time boundaries are not fully documented.
properties.rationale: The external protocol provides specific protection against target-outcome adaptation, supporting a separate partial assessment. It does not automatically establish a complete provenance and leakage audit for the composed pipeline.

criteria_met: Five disjoint patient-level folds are reported, with a common manifest across compared methods.
Hyperparameters, checkpoints, readout regularization, and classification thresholds are validation-selected.
Platt calibrators are fitted on validation patients and applied to the corresponding held-out test patients.
Causal attention and observed-prefix evaluation restrict the predictor to available visits; T3 is identified as a pretraining target rather than a pCR-predictor input.
criteria_missing: A complete audit explicitly excluding held-out trajectories from every pretraining operation is not reported.
Training-only fitting of all treatment-category response-standardization and target-construction statistics is not explicitly documented.
Complete acquisition-versus-availability-time, site/time-overlap, and preprocessing-fit audits are not reported.
properties.rationale: Several concrete split, selection, calibration, and temporal-input controls are implemented. They do not establish the feature's complete leakage-audit criterion. Outcome-free pretraining is not itself evidence of partition isolation. No leakage violation is inferred.

The retained visit history and visit-position embeddings do not establish per-variable elapsed time since true observation. Carry-forward/asynchronous measurement semantics and freshness updates are not described sufficiently to establish presence, absence, or a specific inapplicability dependency.

The paper specifies ordered treatment visits and learned visit-position embeddings, but does not establish retention or reversible availability of actual recorded acquisition times. Visit indexing is not native timestamp retention. Irreversible timestamp deletion is also not established.

scope.time_horizon: Treatment visits T0–T3; elapsed durations not reported

properties.rationale: The model predicts visit states conditional on observed histories and assigned context, but no model or rule is reported for when, whether, or why MRI examinations occur conditional on state or acquisition context. Scheduled trial visits and temporal embeddings alone do not establish observation-process modeling. An explicit ignorable-sampling assumption is not supplied either.

criteria_met: The paper identifies the clinical source collections and their cited releases.
The operational preprocessing description identifies MRI-derived channels, lesion-mask sources, localization fallback, per-visit normalization, cropping/padding, and geometry extraction.
criteria_missing: Measurement-level retention of source identifiers and transformation lineage is not documented.
Actual acquisition and information-availability timestamps are not documented as retained.
Physical measurement units, voxel spacing, and complete unit/conversion provenance are not reported.
properties.rationale: Dataset identity and specified transformations establish part of the provenance responsibility, but not the complete variable-level contract. This automated assessment uses the supplied full text and documented page-image review notes; it does not claim a fresh inspection of PDF bytes or images.

criteria_met: A separate stop-gradient target encoder is updated by EMA, with reported momentum 0.996.
The executed pretraining loss includes SIGReg distributional regularization, with reported weight 0.09, explicitly intended to keep latent representations well spread.
properties.rationale: The source specifies operational anti-collapse mechanisms beyond an algorithm name. Presence denotes their implemented inclusion, not proof that EMA guarantees non-collapse or that a dedicated collapse diagnostic or ablation succeeded.

criteria_met: A four-stage 3-D residual network operationally maps specified MRI volumes to appearance features.
A geometry MLP maps nine lesion descriptors into the shared latent space, and the image and geometry encodings are added.
The resulting 192-dimensional visit representation supplies the history consumed by the conditioned transition.
properties.rationale: The observation-to-representation mapping and executed training configuration are documented. This establishes encoder implementation, not an isolated test of encoder optimality or successful future-state prediction. Comparator-specific ImageNet initialization is not attributed to this encoder.

No named externally pretrained checkpoint is reported as supplying CoRe-WM encoder parameters or features. ImageNet masked-autoencoder initialization belongs to the ViT comparator. CoRe-WM's own self-supervised pretraining and EMA target encoder do not establish foundation-model reuse. Explicit from-scratch initialization is not sufficiently stated to code absence.

criteria_met: The transition predicts a next-visit latent from an observed state prefix and clinical/treatment conditions.
The training target is the separate EMA encoder's next-visit image-plus-geometry representation.
Layer-normalized latent MSE is an explicit term in the executed joint pretraining objective.
properties.rationale: This is an implemented predictive-latent objective, not merely a latent bottleneck or a cited JEPA architecture. Auxiliary descriptor/response losses coexist with it. Downstream pCR and observed-interval probe results do not establish held-out successor-state forecasting accuracy, so implementation is not promoted to forecast evaluation.

scope.time_horizon: One successor visit per observed-prefix training example

properties.rationale: The inspected image pathway predicts EMA target latents rather than reconstructing MRI observations. Its declared objective uses latent prediction and distribution regularization, alongside separate geometry/response prediction tasks. The absence assessment is restricted to MRI observation reconstruction; it does not deny the auxiliary numerical prediction losses or claim that the complete model lacks observed-target supervision.

value.absence_scope: MRI observation reconstruction in the image-encoding/JEPA pathway

criteria_met: MRI appearance and structured clinical information enter a combined computational model.
Image and lesion-descriptor embeddings are combined additively; clinical-profile and assigned-treatment embeddings interact with temporal features through additive conditioning and FiLM.
properties.rationale: The operational combination of imaging and non-imaging clinical information supports multimodal fusion. Lesion geometry is derived from MRI, so its additive combination with appearance, or the eight MRI channels alone, is not treated as sufficient evidence of independently acquired modalities. This assertion establishes the implemented fusion mechanism, not missing-modality robustness or its isolated effectiveness.

The described additive fusion and FiLM pathways do not sufficiently report modality-availability masks, quality or recency weighting, or behavior when imaging or clinical inputs are missing. Enhancement-based localization when a compatible lesion mask is unavailable is a preprocessing fallback, not demonstrated availability-aware fusion. The incomplete missing-input specification does not justify declaring this feature absent.

criteria_met: Defined visit latents and lesion-descriptor histories are retained as ordered prefixes.
The transition consumes the retained prefix to produce a next-visit latent and response state.
Frozen response-state prefixes also feed subsequent pCR readout.
properties.rationale: Persistence is supplied by explicitly retained sequence context rather than an isolated embedding or a claimed recurrent posterior. Executed pretraining and downstream use document implementation; they do not establish held-out successor-state prediction accuracy.

scope.time_horizon: Observed treatment-visit prefix T0 through the current visit

properties.rationale: Scoped architectural absence follows from the documented point-vector formulation: image and geometry encoders produce a latent vector, conditioned Transformers produce point predictions, and training matches these predictions to encoded targets. The maintained state has no posterior or filtering-distribution parameterization in the specified algorithm. SIGReg regularizes the distribution of representations across samples; it is not a conditional belief over an individual patient's hidden state. Logistic pCR probabilities, fold variation, and bootstrap intervals likewise do not turn this state into a belief distribution.

The documented algorithm encodes actual visits into an observed prefix and predicts the next latent from that prefix. It does not provide a distinct operation that corrects a propagated prior state using an arriving observation. The named latent correction adds a geometry-response prediction to the image-path prediction; it is not observation-conditioned filtering correction. This absence is restricted to the specified CoRe-WM algorithm and does not negate its ability to extend context with new visits.

criteria_met: New actual patient visits extend the individual state context at inference.
The pretrained representation model remains frozen while updated prefixes produce revised pCR estimates.
Results are reported at successive observed prefixes in held-out clinical patients.
properties.rationale: This satisfies the broad arriving-evidence update criterion through prefix extension and recomputation, not through a propagate–correct filter. Internal fold-mean pCR AUROC is 0.7337, 0.7545, and 0.7620 at the three prefixes. No assimilation-specific accuracy test or acceptance criterion is reported. The evaluation is retrospective sequential use, not live online deployment.

scope.time_horizon: Successively observed T0, T0–T1, and T0–T2 prefixes

criteria_met: Transferred frozen source models incorporate additional actual visits in individual observed prefixes.
External pCR predictions are reported separately at each prefix without target-outcome fitting.
properties.rationale: Arriving-evidence incorporation is exercised externally, but its existence must not be conflated with benefit: external AUROC decreases from 0.7396 to 0.7321 and 0.7082 as visits are added. The paper does not report an assimilation-specific acceptance test. This is not prospective external system use or proof that updating improves predictions under cohort shift.

scope.time_horizon: Successively observed T0, T0–T1, and T0–T2 prefixes

properties.rationale: The reported inference protocol explicitly freezes the pretrained model and fits a pooled population readout, rather than fitting individual patient parameters. Newly observed MRI changes the patient's context and features, not model weights. Source-only external transfer further retains fitted source models and readouts. This establishes absence of per-patient parameter adaptation in the documented use, not absence of individual history conditioning.

criteria_met: The frozen learned response representation supplies a logistic readout for final pCR.
The same frozen representation supplies a separately fitted ridge probe of observed log-volume shrinkage without defining or retraining a new state model.
properties.rationale: The two typed readouts operate on different summaries of the shared learned state: prefix summaries for pCR in the 808-patient cohort, and T0-to-T2 state change for shrinkage probing in the 791-patient subset. The latter retains a geometric signal already targeted by IRG and includes observed T2; it is not an independent future-state forecast. No general task-reuse acceptance criterion is reported.

criteria_met: Controlled cumulative configurations alter clinical conditioning, treatment conditioning, geometry, response-state factorization, and response guidance.
The configurations share folds, seed, pretraining budget, and frozen-readout protocol and are compared against the same pCR target.
properties.rationale: These are relevant representation/variable ablations, so a state-sufficiency assessment is present. Patient profile gives the largest gain, whereas adding treatment after profile has a reported increment of −0.0019±0.0467. Geometry, FRS, and IRG contribute subsequent gains. The result does not prove a sufficient statistic, isolate order-independent component effects, or establish sufficiency for next-state prediction or treatment selection. Ablation configurations remain distinct from the full model.

scope.time_horizon: Final pCR from the observed T0–T1 prefix

criteria_met: Clinical and treatment inputs are perturbed while MRI latents, geometry, model checkpoints, and the native readout are held fixed.
Held-out pCR discrimination quantifies the resulting dependence on conditioning variables.
properties.rationale: This is a scoped test of which supplied variables contribute to the fitted response representation. Observed-context AUROC is 0.7621±0.0365, versus 0.7329±0.0321 after treatment permutation, 0.6476±0.0210 after clinical-profile permutation, and 0.5951±0.0242 after joint permutation. No sufficiency acceptance criterion is reported. Condition dependence neither proves that all transition determinants are retained nor identifies treatment effects.

scope.time_horizon: Final pCR from the observed T0–T2 prefix

criteria_met: The transition explicitly consumes z_0:t rather than only the current image embedding.
The response pathway processes the individual's lesion-descriptor sequence q_0:t.
Causal attention and positional embeddings preserve prefix order, and the readout uses accumulated response-state summaries.
properties.rationale: Individual observed imaging history affects the inferred response representation through an explicit sequence mechanism. Assigned treatment is shared context rather than a fully specified time-varying action history. This implementation does not by itself prove history-specific personalization beyond generic prognostic priors.

scope.time_horizon: Observed visit history through the current treatment visit

criteria_met: The analysis contrasts correctly supplied patient clinical context with permuted context while holding the patient's MRI, geometry, checkpoint, and readout fixed.
Clinical-profile permutation within treatment families reduces held-out discrimination, providing a limited analogous individual-context control.
criteria_missing: No matched own-versus-swapped or withheld longitudinal imaging-history test establishes the value of the correct individual's trajectory.
No population-prior or adequately prognostic-stratum-matched control separates individualized trajectory value from receptor-subtype, age, and other generic prognostic information.
Complete partition isolation for all pretraining and response-standardization operations is not explicitly audited.
properties.rationale: The reported permutations provide a meaningful but limited context-matching diagnostic. They do not complete the feature's beyond-generic-priors criterion: the paper itself identifies molecular profile and age as the dominant signals and acknowledges correlated treatment/subtype structure. Increasing observed-prefix AUROC and probing volume shrinkage do not substitute for the missing personalization controls.

scope.time_horizon: Final pCR from the observed T0–T2 prefix

properties.rationale: No declared transition memory, constraint, or loss specifically establishes preservation of patient identity or anatomical entities through generated transitions. T0-centered cropping, lesion-morphology supervision, EMA targets, and causal attention have other stated responsibilities and do not alone meet this criterion. No identity-violation evaluation is reported either; therefore neither presence nor absence is established.

criteria_met: The response pathway has documented geometry and imaging-change targets with interpretable lesion-response meaning.
A validation-tuned held-out ridge probe maps frozen state change to observed log-volume shrinkage, and Figure 2d exposes that mapping for inspection.
The probe reports Spearman correlation 0.8623 with 95% CI 0.8347–0.8865 and pooled R² 0.6744 in 791 patients.
criteria_missing: A semantic mapping of the latent state beyond the probed aggregate geometric-response signal is not established.
An operational means for users to inspect individual state variables and their semantic limits is not reported.
properties.rationale: Interpretability is demonstrated only for a bounded geometric-response aspect, not all latent coordinates or a clinically inspectable state service. Actual T2 contributes to the state update, and volume response already contributes to IRG; the probe is therefore representation grounding rather than unseen-future prediction or independent biomarker discovery.

criteria_met: Causal Transformer attention retains access to earlier visit states beyond the current supplied state.
A parallel Transformer retains lesion-descriptor history.
Prefix summaries include initial state, prefix mean, recent revision, and cumulative displacement.
properties.rationale: The specified mechanism is ordered attention context, not an external memory store or recurrent posterior. Its clinical duration and delayed-effect capacity are not reported. The existence of short visit-history memory does not establish useful long-horizon memory.

scope.time_horizon: Short treatment-visit prefixes from four-visit study sequences; downstream pCR inputs extend through T2

criteria_met: Assigned therapy a is explicitly distinguished from baseline clinical profile b and imaging state.
The supplied categorical therapy arm/family is encoded and conditions the transition through additive shifts and FiLM.
Condition-permutation experiments establish that the treatment input can be changed computationally.
properties.rationale: This is an explicit, settable categorical treatment input at implementation stage. Age, receptor status, and MammaPrint remain covariates rather than actions. The assertion does not establish an executable regimen specification, evaluated action-conditioned successor fidelity, causal treatment effects, or clinically supported alternative-regimen comparison.

properties.rationale: The source identifies a therapeutic regimen category separately from baseline covariates, so its treatment meaning is recoverable. However, it does not sufficiently report an operational action-role/effect-channel typing representation or a mechanism distinguishing therapeutic, inquiry, acquisition, or other roles. Therapeutic and physiology labels in the existing ActionSpec are reviewer ontology mappings, not evidence that CoRe-WM implements that typing responsibility. A single therapeutic action family is not itself evidence of absence or a reason for blanket inapplicability.
A conditioned causal Transformer predicts the next visit latent from observed prefix states.
Next-imaging latent transitions are learned with outcome-label-free predictive objectives.
Assigned therapy and clinical profile condition next-state prediction; no unassigned-regimen causal claim.
Frozen response states feed a class-balanced logistic pCR readout.
Next-state predictions operate in JEPA image/geometry response representations.
Fold-validation Platt scaling is evaluated on held-out outcome probabilities; this is not trajectory calibration.

Held-out event-probability calibration reports Brier score, ECE and calibration slope/intercept. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.

criteria_met: The source imaging resource, clinical population, acquisition visits and patient-disjoint partition counts are identified.
Input and target examinations are distinguished, and lesion occupancies are attributed to T0 annotations.
Registration, cropping, resizing, SER transformation and frozen-encoder processing are described.
criteria_missing: The exact archive release and encoder checkpoint identities are not reported.
Complete variable-level provenance, units and acquisition-versus-availability timestamps are not documented.
The observed context variables and precise SER transformation are not sufficiently specified for complete input tracing.
properties.rationale: The paper supplies substantive source and transformation provenance, beyond a dataset name alone, but not the complete variable-level provenance contract. This concerns the reported forecasting pipeline, not an independently inspected provenance service.

The model consumes the elapsed T1-to-target interval, but retention or reversible availability of the actual observation timestamps is not documented. The T0-to-T1 acquisition interval and native timestamp resolution are also unspecified. An elapsed forecast interval does not establish a native-observation timestamp contract.

scope.time_horizon: T0/T1 history to T3; forecast interval represented in days

properties.rationale: Support is derived from prediction-time examinations, and future scans cannot determine crop placement. However, the paper does not distinguish scan acquisition time from the time images, annotations or clinical-context values became usable, or document release-latency-aware queries. Temporal source restrictions are not equivalent to explicit information-availability timestamps.

The documented masks are deliberate history occlusions and anatomical occupancy maps. They do not establish measured/missing/invalid status for naturally unavailable observations. Selection of patients with required examinations and mention of valid evaluation regions likewise do not establish model-input availability masks.

The forecast interval is represented, but no per-variable time-since-measurement representation or freshness update is described. The context variables are incompletely enumerated, so their freshness handling cannot be determined. The global forecast interval is not coded as variable-level measurement age.

scope.time_horizon: T0/T1 conditioning examinations and one T3 target

criteria_met: The patient-specific elapsed forecast interval enters the observed context.
The forecast interval modulates the spatial blocks and explicitly scales the neural correction through s(Delta t).
properties.rationale: Real elapsed clinical time affects the implemented prediction rather than serving only as a visit label. This establishes interval-aware one-step forecasting, not continuous-time integration or complete handling of irregular history. No time-input ablation or interval-stratified validation is reported.

scope.time_horizon: Delta t = T3 acquisition time minus T1 acquisition time, measured in days

properties.rationale: The paper describes the source trial's examination schedule and includes elapsed time and unspecified acquisition/clinical context. It does not sufficiently describe a conditional model or operational rule for when, whether or why measurements occur. A schedule description, context embedding and occlusion masks do not by themselves establish this feature.

P³ audits history use, supplied spatial support and comparison with a population-average correction. It does not report a temporal-grid witness-preservation audit across sampled values, update patterns, native timing and external acquisition channels. Spatial resizing or a zero-occupancy exclusion is not such an audit.

Registration to T0, resizing, a fixed SER transform and projection to a common latent grid are reported. Source-specific units, terminology or measurement definitions mapped through traceable conversions to a declared semantic schema are not documented. Spatial alignment alone does not meet this feature's criterion.

criteria_met: Training, validation and test partitions are reported as patient-disjoint.
RRR shrinkage, rank, regularization, standardization and dimensionality reduction are fitted within the corresponding training partition.
The RRR and neural correction are fitted on training patients and frozen for the reported audit.
T0 determines the reference, disease-bed crop and supplied annotations; future examinations cannot determine crop placement.
criteria_missing: Validation was previously used during development, so the reported comparisons do not constitute untouched held-out confirmation.
Encoder-pretraining overlap with study patients is not documented.
Complete availability checks for the unspecified acquisition/clinical context are not reported.
Site/time overlap checks and a comprehensive executed leakage audit are not reported.
properties.rationale: Several explicit leakage-aware preparation mechanisms are implemented, but comprehensive assurance is incomplete. Reused validation limits independence; it does not by itself prove that future targets entered training or justify an assertion of actual leakage. No result is reported on the listed test partition.

The source is a public multicenter imaging resource, but no site-local training/query protocol, exchanged artifacts or federated aggregation is described. Multicenter origin does not establish federation, and the paper does not explicitly document an incompatible identifiable-record pooling mechanism sufficient for an absence assertion.

criteria_met: Frozen 3DINO maps resized volumetric SER MRI to a 1024 × 7 × 7 × 7 spatial representation.
These representations supply the longitudinal context and future target used in the reported forecasting experiments.
properties.rationale: An operational observation-to-representation mapping is specified and used, rather than merely cited. Forecast evaluation does not independently establish encoder quality, clinical state sufficiency or the capabilities of the separately cited 3DINO study.

criteria_met: The reused encoder is named as 3DINO and associated with the Xu et al. 2025 reference.
Its used role and output dimensions are specified.
Adaptation status is explicit: the image encoder remains frozen.
criteria_missing: The exact pretrained checkpoint, weight version or immutable artifact identifier is not reported.
properties.rationale: Named pretrained-representation reuse is documented, but checkpoint-level provenance is insufficient for the feature's complete version-pinned criterion. No pretraining objective, cohort independence or performance is inherited from the cited encoder paper.

criteria_met: The neural correction is trained against a frozen future-examination latent target.
The loss uses channel-averaged smooth-L1 error on occluded, core-occupied latent tokens, normalized within patient.
The objective does not require decoding or reconstructing MRI pixels.
properties.rationale: The operational training objective predicts a target representation. This is not merely the presence of a latent bottleneck. The image encoder itself is not trained by this objective, and superiority over reconstruction-based training was not tested.

scope.time_horizon: One T3 target representation from T0/T1 history

criteria_met: The shared image encoder defining context and target representations is frozen during Cancer JEPA fitting.
Consequently, the target representation cannot jointly adapt toward a trivial constant through the Cancer JEPA training objective.
properties.rationale: The positive assessment is narrowly scoped to the explicit fixed-target constraint preventing joint encoder/target collapse during this training stage. This is reviewer interpretation of the frozen-encoder mechanism, not an author-reported anti-collapse experiment. It does not establish that the pretrained representation is noncollapsed in every relevant sense, or that the trainable correction cannot underuse context. Occlusion discouraging copying is a separate mechanism and is not treated as proof of collapse prevention.

The documented Cancer JEPA objective compares predicted and frozen target representations rather than reconstructed observations. The paper explicitly distinguishes its endpoint from a future MRI image. This scoped absence concerns raw-observation reconstruction during Cancer JEPA training, not the unknown pretraining objectives of the reused 3DINO encoder and not reconstruction of latent quantities.

Criterion requires at least two separately identified modalities in a fusion operation. The implemented correction combines MRI latents, longitudinal differences, MRI-derived core/ring occupancy and non-spatial context using projections and context modulation. Multiple timepoints and derived maps of MRI are not independent modalities. The observed acquisition/clinical context a_i is not enumerated enough to establish a distinct second modality in the evaluated configuration. Thus combined-input processing is explicit, but multimodal fusion under this criterion remains unresolved after source review, not unassessed or proven absent.

properties.rationale: Acquisition time is described, but reconstruction completion or other information-release times are not distinguished from acquisition. The paper does not document availability-aware training-query construction.

The methods do not specify when reconstructed images or lesion-localization information become available to an intended noncontrast query. Acquisition timestamps alone do not establish information-availability semantics.

Observed acquisition times and generated intermediate times are distinguished in the LDL construction, but no measured/missing/invalid indicator supplied to the prediction model is reported. Sparse-time interpolation is not itself an availability mask.

The breast preprocessing and generator descriptions do not report missingness or image-validity masks consumed by the model. Lesion cropping and the observed-versus-virtual time construction do not establish this feature.

The baseline-to-query elapsed time is represented globally. No per-variable or per-measurement freshness representation, carry-forward policy, or freshness update mechanism is reported; the global time condition is insufficient for this criterion.

Requested elapsed time conditions generation from one baseline image, but measurement-specific age and updating under asynchronous observations are not described. Neither presence nor an incompatible carry-forward implementation is established.

Actual elapsed time conditions image generation through CLIP, while LDL explicitly uses unequal adjacent time gaps in its temporal penalty. This establishes an implemented irregular-time mechanism, not accuracy at every unobserved time, continuous-time physiological integration, or a validated effective horizon.

properties.rationale: The paper describes manually controlled sparse acquisition and uses acquired times as conditions, but reports no conditional rule or model for when, whether or why an observation occurs. Time conditioning and synthetic densification alone do not satisfy the observation-process criterion.

Acquisition variability, scanner descriptions and the reported median intersequence interval characterize the data, but no observation-occurrence or informative-missingness model conditional on patient/acquisition context is reported.

Sparse sampling motivates the method, but no target-specific grid witness-preservation audit across values, update patterns, native timing and external acquisition channels is reported. LDL smoothness and generated renal curves are different assessments.

The breast experiments do not define and test an observation-clock witness distinction at a specified grid resolution. Adjacent-frame cSSIM and three-timepoint lesion examples do not establish such an audit.

Registration, resizing and normalization are reported, but source-specific measurement definitions and intensity units are not mapped through traceable conversions to a declared semantic/unit schema. Common tensor dimensions and an output normalization range alone do not establish this feature.

Multiple scanner manufacturers and field strengths are described, but no source-specific semantic or intensity-unit harmonization contract is reported. The relationship between normalized inputs and the intensity scale used for rMSE remains insufficiently specified.

Different training/test acquisition times are mentioned, but patient/slice partitioning, overlap checks, training-only preprocessing fits and validation-only hyperparameter selection are not reported. The description does not establish either leakage control or actual leakage.

Examination/patient/slice separation, repeated-examination overlap, lesion-location availability and training-only preprocessing/model selection are not audited in the reported protocol. A distinction between training and test times does not establish these controls.

No site-local data-retention arrangement, federated training/query procedure or exchanged-artifact protocol is reported. A private dataset and an A100 training-hardware description establish neither federation nor explicit identifiable-record central pooling.

Use of a public imaging resource is reported without a federated execution or data-access protocol. Public availability and scanner diversity do not establish federation, privacy guarantees or its explicit absence.

The baseline image is operationally encoded through the zero-convolution conditioning pathway, whose features enter latent-diffusion layers. CLIP encodes the time condition. Execution is supported by the implementation description and reported model experiments, but encoder-specific effectiveness is not separately tested.

The separately trained breast configuration uses the described image-condition encoder and CLIP time-conditioning pathway. An operational observation-to-feature mapping is established; this does not establish a persistent clinical belief state or encoder robustness.

The complete reported objectives are diffusion noise regression plus LAL template-distance regularization, followed by diffusion noise regression plus LDL temporal-difference regularization. The template aggregates generated latent statistics, and LDL penalizes derivatives; neither supplies a context-to-target representation prediction term. Latent diffusion and a VAE bottleneck do not themselves satisfy this predictive-latent feature. This assessment does not assert anything about unreported pretraining of inherited encoders.

criteria_met: The MRI source cohorts are identified as ADNI, OASIS-3 and AIBL.
The executed preprocessing chain and use of longitudinal acquisition-time differences are described.
criteria_missing: Measurement-level retention of source and transformation lineage is not documented.
Dataset release identities, information-availability timestamps and a complete unit/schema provenance contract are not reported.
properties.rationale: This is limited source and transformation provenance, not evidence of a complete operational M1 provenance service. Naming cohorts and describing processing do not establish traceability of every derived measurement.

criteria_met: The longitudinal latent observations are indexed by imaging capture time.
Observed endpoint time differences enter the velocity target, and baseline age plus elapsed span anchors prediction.
properties.rationale: Presence is scoped to acquisition time at the modeled longitudinal resolution, not device-level timestamp preservation. The numerical integration step dt=0.01 is not treated as a native measurement cadence or as having established physical units.

scope.time_horizon: Longitudinal acquisition-time coordinates and elapsed years; raw scanner timestamp precision is not reported.

properties.rationale: The supplied full text does not distinguish MRI or metadata acquisition time from the time those inputs became usable. In particular, baseline versus future clinical-status conditioning and its availability are insufficiently specified. This does not establish that future information actually leaked.

No model input encoding measured, missing or invalid MRI/metadata values is described. Skull stripping, image cropping and reported registration failures do not establish missingness or validity masks supplied to the model. Failure exclusions and invalid-input handling remain unspecified.

Elapsed forecast time and baseline age are represented, but per-variable freshness of MRI-derived or clinical metadata measurements is not described. A global prediction interval does not establish time-since-observation tracking for individual inputs.

criteria_met: The training velocity target divides latent displacement by the observed endpoint time difference.
The forecast integrates over the requested interval and conditions on start, current and end query times.
properties.rationale: Actual elapsed intervals affect prediction rather than being replaced solely by uniform visit indices. This implementation assessment does not establish a dedicated irregular-sampling robustness test, calibrated clinical-time dynamics or accurate prediction at every arbitrary interval. The paper's progression-coordinate qualification remains unresolved.

scope.time_horizon: Requested longitudinal intervals; quantitative forecasting results extend to 13 years.

properties.rationale: The method uses observed capture times and externally specified forecast times, but no rule or model for when, whether or why follow-up imaging occurs is reported. Different follow-up availability across subjects is acknowledged without an observation-generation model. Time conditioning alone does not satisfy this feature.

No target-specific temporal-grid witness-preservation audit is reported. Spatial MRI resampling, future-horizon analysis and additive residual-noise sensitivity do not test preservation across sampled values, update patterns, native timing and external acquisition channels.

criteria_met: MRI observations undergo a common spatial and intensity preprocessing chain, including resampling, tissue-contrast normalization and registration to a standard brain template.
criteria_missing: Source-specific measurement mappings, traceable conversion records and the target template/schema identity are not sufficiently specified.
The reported '1.5 mm3 voxels' wording does not unambiguously establish voxel spacing versus volume.
Scanner/protocol harmonization and scanner-invariant representations remain proposed future work rather than evaluated source-invariance mechanisms.
properties.rationale: Only the imaging-standardization subset is established. It is not a complete semantic/unit harmonization contract, and reported orientation inconsistencies and registration failures limit any assurance of correct mapping.

The random 80/5/15 split is not accompanied by the patient/scan/pair partition unit, longitudinal-overlap controls, training-only preprocessing/template fitting or an information-availability audit. Clinical-status availability is also unclear. A nominal split alone is insufficient, but these omissions do not demonstrate leakage.

No site-local training or query protocol, exchanged artifacts or federated aggregation mechanism is described. Using three clinical datasets does not establish federation. The paper also does not supply the explicit identifiable-record pooling evidence required for the feature's absence rule.

criteria_met: An AE/VAE encoder maps an observed baseline MRI to the latent state consumed by the velocity model.
Executed training settings and encoder-capacity/crop ablations document use of the mapping.
properties.rationale: The operational observation-to-state mapping is established by the reported pipeline and experiments. The AE/VAE terminology does not establish a posterior-belief filter, complete VAE objective or predictive uncertainty.

Appendix C explicitly states that the default comparison does not use a pretrained AE. This scoped absence concerns transferred encoder parameters in the default configuration, not the separately reported MAISI-initialization experiment.

criteria_met: The flow-training loss regresses a latent-space velocity target constructed from earlier and later encoded MRI representations.
The target is longitudinal latent displacement divided by elapsed time rather than raw MRI reconstruction for this objective.
properties.rationale: This establishes the functional latent-prediction objective in the dynamics-training stage. It does not classify the AE pretraining as JEPA, imply joint encoder/predictor co-training or exclude a separate observation-reconstruction objective.

criteria_met: The ArcRank representation-learning design includes a positive-margin chronological ranking constraint that penalizes equal or insufficiently separated magnitudes.
A stop-gradient operation is applied in the paired representation objective.
The paper explicitly relates removal of the ranking margin to latent mode collapse.
properties.rationale: Specified anti-triviality and training-stabilization mechanisms are present in the representation stage used by the predictive system. This is not a proof of collapse prevention: the authors also report collapse for excessive angular-loss weights and convergence problems for excessive ranking weights. No universal or independently validated collapse-free guarantee is assigned.

criteria_met: The first-stage encoder-decoder reconstructs observed MRI, with an image-loss pathway shown in Figure 1.
The reported reconstruction trade-offs and AE configuration experiments document training and use of this reconstruction mapping.
properties.rationale: Observation reconstruction is an implemented first-stage objective alongside ArcRank. The complete loss formula, weighting and any KL component are insufficiently specified, so no particular reconstruction norm or fully specified VAE objective is inferred. Reconstruction and the separate latent velocity-regression objective coexist.

criteria_met: MRI-derived latent representations interact with separately identified structured patient metadata.
Condition-processing MLPs generate AdaLN parameters applied within the U-Net decoder layers.
Reported metadata perturbation experiments corroborate operational use of the conditioning inputs.
properties.rationale: The fusion is between imaging representations and structured patient attributes, not between the three MRI datasets. Temporal query embeddings are not counted as another clinical modality. This assertion establishes the implemented interaction, not missing-modality robustness or clinically valid conditioning.

The paper specifies metadata/time conditioning through AdaLN but does not specify availability masks, quality/recency-dependent fusion, or behavior when MRI or conditioning metadata are missing. Sex flipping and clinical-status noise are not missing-modality tests. A requirement that all inputs be present is also not explicitly established, so absence is not asserted.

criteria_met: An observed MRI initializes a defined latent state.
Each numerical transition carries the preceding latent state into the next velocity-field update.
The propagated terminal state is decoded and evaluated against later observed MRI.
properties.rationale: Persistence is established by the executed latent integration and reported future-observation results, not merely by the presence of an encoder. Numerical integration steps are distinguished from years of follow-up. The evidence does not establish a tolerance-validated horizon or independent patient-level splitting.

No observation-history-conditioned filtering distribution with stated uncertainty semantics is reported. The AE/VAE terminology and stochastic-flow preliminaries do not establish such a belief. Conversely, deterministic propagation conditional on an initialized latent does not resolve the encoder's latent-distribution convention sufficiently to assert that every state representation is exclusively deterministic.

The specified forecast procedure encodes the baseline once, repeatedly propagates its latent state, and decodes the requested endpoint. It contains no operation accepting a newly measured observation to correct a prior prediction. This is scoped absence of a correction operation in the documented open-loop query, not a claim that the architecture could never be extended with filtering.

Within the fully described inference episode, subsequent states derive from the baseline initialization and generated latent updates, without later measured scans entering the rollout. Numerical state updates are not assimilation of arriving evidence. Reinitializing a separate forecast from another scan would not itself demonstrate sequential assimilation.

The reported inference algorithm evaluates the trained encoder, condition-processing networks, velocity field and decoder; it updates the latent state rather than fitting individual parameters or model weights. Patient-specificity is supplied through baseline representations, metadata and training regularization. No parameter-fitting operation occurs in this documented inference path. This assertion does not exclude an unreported alternative adaptation procedure.

The demonstrated output is future MRI generation. Multiple horizons, several image-error metrics and t-SNE coloring by diagnosis do not establish a second typed task/readout sharing the same learned state checkpoint. The paper also does not document separately trained task-specific state models that would establish the feature's negative criterion.

criteria_met: Conditioning is removed in an unconditional-versus-conditional comparison against the MRI prediction targets.
Angular, ranking and combined latent-representation training strategies are compared using image and progression-error metrics.
AE capacity and crop-size variants are evaluated against forecasting metrics.
properties.rationale: These are relevant representation/input ablations under this feature's operational definition, not proof that the learned state contains every transition determinant. Outcomes are metric-dependent: ArcRank with temporal sampling improves several reported means but has lower SSIM than ArcRank with normalized sampling. No history-length sufficiency, causal sufficiency or clinical decision-sufficiency conclusion follows.

The documented inference interface uses one supplied baseline MRI and attributes/time queries, rather than conditioning on a sequence of earlier individual scans or actions. Longitudinal pairs supervise training but are not a patient's inference-time history. Here baseline conditioning is distinguished from conditioning on history preceding that supplied snapshot, consistent with the feature's explicit current-snapshot exclusion.

scope.time_horizon: Inference initialized from one observed MRI

properties.rationale: No matched individual-history swap/withholding or population-prior forecast control is reported. Patient clustering, ArcRank ablations, general conditioning removal and sex/status perturbations do not isolate the added predictive value of the correct individual's information without leakage. Personalization is claimed and structurally encouraged, but the specified audit is not established.

criteria_met: ArcRank explicitly aligns the directions of longitudinal representations belonging to the same patient.
The authors assign latent direction the role of preserving patient identity.
The regularizer is part of the reported trained configuration, not solely a proposed extension.
properties.rationale: This establishes an implemented identity-consistency loss mechanism. It does not establish anatomically faithful identity preservation at every generated horizon. The reported ablations and t-SNE visualization do not substitute for a dedicated decoded-identity violation test.

criteria_met: The authors document a global semantic interpretation of latent direction as patient identity and magnitude as progression stage.
SVD-derived components and t-SNE plots provide an inspectable representation-level visualization.
Figure 3 displays ADNI representations colored by patient identity and diagnosis.
criteria_missing: The proposed progression-stage interpretation is not resolved into a validated mapping to measured clinical severity; chronology is imposed and clinical-status conditioning creates a stage-specific interpretation ambiguity.
No readable mapping from propagated latent components to identified anatomical or physiological variables is supplied.
properties.rationale: The representation has inspectable global structure, but qualitative projected clustering does not make the full state physiologically interpretable. No clinician interpretation study or clinical severity readout is inferred.

The specified transition uses the current propagated latent, time and patient attributes. It contains no recurrent history store, earlier-observation context window or external memory beyond that supplied state. Sinusoidal time embeddings and numerical state persistence are not additional observation-history memory. This is not a finding that a Markov state is intrinsically inadequate.

The documented prediction interface comprises an MRI-derived latent, temporal queries and patient attributes, with no settable treatment, acquisition command or other intervention separated from observed state. Flipping sex and perturbing diagnostic status are metadata sensitivity experiments, not executable clinical actions. A requested forecast time specifies the observation target rather than an intervention on the modeled patient.

properties.applicability_reason: The documented model is an actionless observational MRI forecaster. Because its assessed prediction interface has no clinical action variable, distinguishing action roles and effect channels within an action vocabulary is inapplicable to this configuration.
properties.rationale: This dependency-specific inapplicability does not treat metadata as an uninterpreted action vector and does not extend to any future treatment-conditioned version.

criteria_met: The institution, collection period, patient-linked imaging inputs, tumor delineations, and survival information are identified.
Baseline and target MRI acquisition are distinguished relative to surgery and radiotherapy initiation.
The patient-level partition and dataset sample units are reported.
criteria_missing: Variable-level acquisition and information-availability timestamps are not documented as retained model-accessible provenance.
Scanner/protocol identifiers, physical voxel units, intensity transformations, and traceable registration or slice-correspondence transformations are not reported.
A versioned source-data or preprocessing provenance record is not described.
properties.rationale: This is partial documentation of patient-linked source and temporal provenance, shared by the four LDM configurations. It does not establish a complete operational variable-level provenance service.

The collection period and relative scan timing are reported, but retention or reversible availability of each patient's actual scan dates and baseline-to-target interval is not established. The nominal four-month target is not evidence of native timestamp retention.

scope.time_horizon: Baseline MRI before radiotherapy to MRI acquired four months after radiotherapy began

properties.rationale: The baseline-input configurations use pre-treatment MRI/GTV, with predicted survival added in pred 2-class. The paper does not describe information-release timestamps, delineation availability latency, or queries audited against those timestamps. The survival classifier's development partition is also unspecified.

The GTV mask identifies tumor location; it is not a missingness or measurement-validity indicator. No mechanism distinguishing missing or invalid MRI/GTV values from observed values is described. Selection of paired scans does not establish such a mechanism.

properties.applicability_reason: The documented inference operation has no carried-forward clinical measurements or asynchronously refreshed variables whose per-variable age must be updated. It consumes a fixed baseline MRI/GTV pair for one future-image query. This does not make actual scan timing or information-availability timing inapplicable.

scope.time_horizon: One future MRI generated from a fixed baseline image/mask pair

properties.rationale: The algorithm does not expose real elapsed clinical time as an input. Actual interval variability and its handling are not reported, so uniform spacing with ignored known unequal intervals is not asserted. Diffusion indices, DDIM steps, and epochs do not establish irregular clinical-time handling.

scope.time_horizon: Nominal target four months after radiotherapy initiation

properties.rationale: The paper describes scan selection, scheduled follow-up, and tumor-containing slice inclusion, but not a model of when, whether, or why observations occur conditional on patient or acquisition state. Selection rules are not themselves a modeled observation-generation process.

No target-specific temporal witness-preservation experiment across sampled values, update/validity patterns, native timing, and external channels is reported. A four-month target and image-similarity evaluation do not establish an observation-clock audit or a clock regime.

The modality and 256×256 image matrix are identified, but no traceable mapping of source-specific measurement definitions, scanner protocols, physical units, or intensity scales to a declared target schema is reported. Equal latent dimensions concern tensor concatenation, not semantic or unit harmonization.

criteria_met: An 80%/10%/10% patient-level training/validation/test partition is reported.
The VQ-VAE and LDM test sets are explicitly identical.
This configuration does not receive a survival-class condition.
criteria_missing: Training-only fitting of all preprocessing and transformations is not documented.
An information-release audit for baseline inputs is not reported.
Image correspondence and selection procedures are not documented sufficiently for a complete leakage audit.
properties.rationale: Patient-level separation is a substantive control, but it does not by itself establish every feature-availability and preprocessing condition. Classifier-partition uncertainty is not assigned to this no-class configuration.

A local single-center dataset and training hardware are described, but no federated participants, local training/query protocol, or exchanged artifacts are reported. Single-center provenance alone is not an explicit negative statement about federation and does not establish privacy controls.

criteria_met: A trained MRI VQ-VAE maps pre-treatment MRI slices into quantized latent representations.
A separate trained GTV VQ-VAE maps tumor masks into compatible latent representations.
These representations are operational conditioning inputs to the evaluated future-image generator.
properties.rationale: The shared encoding responsibility is implemented in the four configurations. This does not establish a persistent clinical belief state, foundation-checkpoint reuse, or missing-modality robustness.

The paper reports trained MRI/GTV VQ-VAEs and a pretrained ResNet-based classifier learned on the same cohort, but identifies no transferred foundation-encoder checkpoint/version or adaptation protocol. An implementation based on Stable Diffusion does not establish transfer of Stable Diffusion encoder parameters. Conversely, training on this cohort does not explicitly establish training from scratch.

Absent for the described LDM training objective: Algorithm 1 minimizes error in predicting sampled Gaussian corruption noise, not error against a target patient/image representation predicted from context. The use of quantized latents and conditional denoising does not itself establish a JEPA-style representation-prediction objective. This conclusion concerns the specified LDM loss, not unreported auxiliary encoder losses.

No specified representation-collapse prevention term, constraint, proof, or collapse diagnostic is reported for these learned representations. The generic discussion of avoiding GAN mode collapse concerns a different phenomenon. A VQ-VAE codebook or the name of a cited method does not establish the actual anti-collapse training mechanism.

Absent specifically as an observed-image reconstruction loss in the supplied LDM training algorithm: its written objective compares predicted noise with sampled Gaussian noise. Decoding generated latents and computing image-similarity metrics at evaluation do not turn that objective into an observed-image reconstruction loss. This does not establish absence of reconstruction training in the separately trained autoencoders.

criteria_met: Imaging representations and an actual clinical survival-outcome category jointly condition generation.
MRI/GTV latents enter concatenation; the survival-class embedding enters U-Net cross-attention.
properties.rationale: This is implemented imaging–clinical-label fusion, not proof of a beneficial fusion effect. The ground-truth survival category is hindsight information, not a baseline-available clinical modality.

scope.time_horizon: One MRI target four months after radiotherapy initiation

properties.rationale: The paper describes MRI/GTV latent concatenation but no availability, quality, or recency conditioning and no missing-image or missing-GTV behavior. The designed omission of survival conditioning in this ablation is not an availability-aware inference mechanism.

A baseline representation is retained as conditioning, but the source does not clearly define it as an evolving clinical state carried into a subsequent clinical prediction/update. Recurrence of the noisy target latent is computational denoising, not clinical-state persistence. An explicit clinical predecessor/successor state interface would resolve the identity question.

scope.time_horizon: Baseline MRI to one four-month post-radiotherapy-start MRI target

properties.rationale: The described baseline-state path encodes and quantizes MRI/GTV into conditioning tensors; it does not maintain a posterior/filtering distribution over hidden clinical state. Gaussian initialization and reverse diffusion generate future images and are not a maintained state belief. Absence is restricted to this documented inference mechanism.

The documented inference generates a future image from fixed baseline conditioning and contains no correction operation using a newly measured clinical observation. Reverse-diffusion denoising is not observation assimilation. This scoped absence is not a claim that a forecaster requires filtering.
The complete described prediction uses one baseline MRI/GTV and does not receive later measured observations. No current patient state is sequentially updated during this inference operation.

scope.time_horizon: Fixed baseline to one future MRI

properties.rationale: Population training updates theta, whereas the supplied inference algorithm only applies the trained denoiser to patient inputs and updates the sampled target latent. It contains no individual parameter-fitting or weight-update rule. This absence is restricted to the described inference path.

The shared MRI VQ-VAE encodes pre/post image domains, but the paper does not establish one maintained state feeding at least two typed prediction tasks/readouts. Reconstruction scores and several metrics of the same generated image do not establish this feature.

criteria_met: A no-survival-condition configuration is compared against predicted and observed survival-conditioned configurations.
Whole-image and local future-image metrics are reported for the omitted conditioning variable.
properties.rationale: This satisfies the narrow variable-ablation form of the definition, not proof of a sufficient persistent clinical state. It does not test omission of baseline anatomy, multi-visit history, or treatment determinants.

criteria_met: The individual's pre-target MRI and GTV explicitly condition the future-image forecast through encoded latent concatenation.
properties.rationale: Presence is narrowly baseline-observation conditioning: one prior clinical timepoint relative to the forecast. It does not establish multi-visit history integration, extra temporal memory, persistent-state semantics, or a measured personalization advantage.

No matched baseline-image/GTV swap, withholding, or population-prior control tests the value of the correct individual's information. Removing survival conditioning leaves individual anatomy intact and is not that audit.

Baseline MRI/GTV conditioning is intended to guide structure and tumor location, but no identity/anatomy-preserving memory, constraint, or loss is specified. Shared encoding and reconstruction quality do not establish the required transition-consistency mechanism.

MRI and the input GTV have recognizable semantics, but the learned quantized state codes have no reported entity/physiology mapping or state-inspection procedure. Viewing decoded images is not by itself inspectable latent-state semantics.

The described model uses one supplied baseline MRI/GTV rather than a history beyond that snapshot. The complete inference contains no clinical recurrent memory, visit context, or historical action sequence. Denoising iteration state is not extra clinical history memory.

The documented no-class inputs are MRI/GTV conditioning and target-generation noise. No treatment choice, dose, schedule, or executable command enters the prediction. Being paired before/after observed care does not make treatment a settable model input.

properties.applicability_reason: The inspected model has no action input, as recorded in assertion:B021:api16:f15-no-class. MRI and GTV are observation/localization inputs, leaving no modeled action roles or effect channels to type.

The structural predictor's embedding and transformer architecture are described without a named pretrained encoder checkpoint. Equation (6) explicitly trains conditional rectified-flow velocity matching on encoded video latents. This establishes latent generative training, but not unambiguously a context-to-target representation-learning objective in the feature's JEPA-style sense. Resolution requires clarifying whether latent denoising/velocity targets alone satisfy this feature; no separate predictive representation loss is reported. A latent tokenizer alone is not treated as sufficient.

The explicitly described warm start predicts a clean future representation against a teacher-trajectory endpoint without requiring decoded-observation reconstruction for that objective. Presence is limited to this training subobjective; it does not establish JEPA encoder pretraining, a learned target encoder, anti-collapse validation or a separately measured benefit from the warm start.

The completion subobjective reconstructs masked current structural observations using Smooth-L1 and is weighted in the joint predictor loss. The supplied methods describe volume, goal-slice, and rendered-slice encoders, but do not specify measured/missing/invalid indicators, valid-field masks, or treatment of invalid sampled pixels. Partial observability and switching between posterior training and prior-only inference do not themselves establish an input validity mask.

properties.applicability_reason: Reported inference starts with the complete volume and target slice, encodes them once, and introduces no newly arriving measured inputs during refinement. The evaluated algorithm does not query a clinical timeline with differing collection and release times.
properties.rationale: This applicability judgment concerns the fixed-input offline protocol only. It does not establish correct information-release handling for intraoperative streaming, delayed data, or a future clinical deployment.

properties.applicability_reason: The reported preprocessing resamples spatial volumes and extracts spatial slices. It does not map a native observation-time stream onto a temporal sampling grid or define a target distinction between acquisition histories. The target/grid dependencies of an observation-clock witness audit are not present in this evaluated offline registration query.
properties.rationale: Spatial resampling should not be confused with temporal gridding. This judgment does not claim that spatial preprocessing preserves all registration evidence.

No site-local training/query protocol, exchanged artifacts, aggregation procedure, or federated access mechanism is described. Public dataset use and experiments on one A800 GPU neither establish federation nor prove that a federation mechanism is absent.

Dataset-specific tensor dimensions and mm/degree metric units are reported, but source-to-target unit conversions, voxel-spacing mappings, pose-frame harmonization, and a traceable common semantic schema are not. Spatial resizing and naming units do not establish the specified harmonization feature.

properties.applicability_reason: The modeled successor coordinate is an internal pose-refinement step. Training paths are synthesized over L indices, and reported inference performs a fixed number of internal updates. No unequal elapsed acquisition intervals are part of this evaluated transition problem.
properties.rationale: Pose increments are spatial action parameters, not delta-time inputs. This does not establish irregular-time support for future live acquisition.

scope.time_horizon: Pose/refinement steps, not elapsed clinical time

properties.rationale: The paper names the official CAMUS split and fixed evaluation slices, but does not explain its independent partitioning unit, participant overlap checks, 3D-volume construction, or training-only fitting of preprocessing. A named official split alone is insufficient to establish the operational leakage-control criteria. No actual leakage is inferred.

properties.rationale: The reported case-level boundary supplies a concrete subset of leakage safeguards. It does not establish a complete patient-independent preparation audit, and fixed test sampling primarily supports reproducibility rather than proving non-leakage.

properties.applicability_reason: The evaluated inference procedure uses fixed image context and internally generated latent updates, not asynchronously refreshed variables or carried-forward measurements on a clinical-time axis. Per-variable elapsed time since observation has no defined role in this reported query.
properties.rationale: Repeated use of the fixed target and volume is intentional task conditioning, not evidence that carried physiological measurements are being treated as current.

properties.applicability_reason: The evaluated query registers a fixed target slice to a fixed volume through pose-indexed computational refinement. Its transition coordinate is not an acquired temporal sequence, and no actual acquisition-time resolution is modeled. Native clinical timestamp retention is therefore inapplicable to this narrowly scoped registration mechanism, not established as absent from the source datasets.
properties.rationale: Synthetic trajectory indices and refinement counts must not be recoded as recorded observation timestamps. This disposition does not extend to the proposed future streaming or robotic application.

properties.rationale: DreamReg specifies pose-dependent slice rendering and an observation-conditioned training posterior. These describe observation content and latent inference. They do not sufficiently specify a model of when, whether, or why measured observations occur conditional on state or acquisition context. Rendering one training slice at every synthesized step is not evidence of a learned clinical acquisition-occurrence process; reported inference receives no new measurements.

The paper excludes the goal embedding from latent dynamics to discourage direct final-pose shortcut learning. It does not specify this as preventing collapsed or trivial representations, nor report a collapse diagnostic, variance constraint, target-network mechanism, or anti-collapse property. Reconstruction and KL losses alone are not evidence of a separately established anti-collapse mechanism.

properties.rationale: The encoders are specified as components of the executed registration system. Final registration results establish system execution, not a separate encoder-quality evaluation. Layer widths and pretrained-checkpoint status remain unreported.

The paper specifies 2D and 3D CNN encoders but names no transferred encoder checkpoint, version, or adaptation procedure. criteria_met: The learned prior predicts z_t from previous belief, pose increment, current pose, and volume context without the current rendered slice.

The rollout-averaged KL divergence between posterior and prior trains agreement in latent-distribution space, separately from the image-reconstruction term.
properties.rationale: This meets the supplied broad latent-target prediction criterion through a sequential, action-conditioned prior/posterior matching objective, rather than through a VAE bottleneck alone. The complete system also uses reconstruction, reward, and pose losses. No separate JEPA-style encoder pretraining, fixed target encoder, or direct latent-prediction accuracy result is established.
properties.value: Action-conditioned latent-distribution prediction through posterior–prior KL matching; not a claim of JEPA pretraining.

criteria_met: The decoder reconstructs a rendered training slice from recurrent belief, stochastic latent, and goal context.

The CAMUS ablation removes reconstruction supervision and reports final registration metrics against the full method.
properties.rationale: Reconstruction is implemented, and its contribution is evaluated through the CAMUS loss ablation. Table 2 reports DisErr 7.33±0.12 mm without reconstruction versus 7.16±0.13 mm for the full method, and SSIM 50.12±0.73% versus 51.87±0.35%. These are final registration outcomes, not direct prior-only imagined-slice fidelity measurements. No declared acceptance test or statistical significance result is reported.

criteria_met: The reported training procedure includes a decoded-slice L1-plus-SSIM reconstruction loss.

properties.rationale: Reconstruction implementation is supported for the µ-RegPro configuration. properties.applicability_reason: The reported perception inputs are ultrasound volumes and ultrasound slices, rather than two independently identified observation modalities. properties.rationale: Separate 2D and 3D ultrasound encoders and concatenation operations are implemented, but multiple dimensional representations of ultrasound do not alone establish multimodal fusion.

properties.applicability_reason: The scoped encoder has no demonstrated multimodal-fusion operation to make availability-aware: its image inputs are all ultrasound, while poses are control/context variables. properties.rationale: This dependency-based assessment does not establish robustness to missing input volumes, missing goal slices, or poor ultrasound quality.

criteria_met: Source cohorts and the wearable origin of measurements are identified.
Feature definitions, selected measurement units, weekly aggregation and pretraining-derived normalization are described.
Evaluation participants are distinguished from the world-model pretraining population.
criteria_missing: Variable-level records retaining acquisition and information-availability times through preprocessing are not established.

A complete provenance contract linking individual decoded predictions to source measurements is not established.
properties.rationale: The paper documents meaningful source and transformation provenance, but not all required variable-level temporal and version metadata. Dataset names alone are not treated as sufficient.

The inspected preprocessing describes minute-level/daily source measurements aggregated onto weekly or ISO-calendar-week representations. It does not establish whether actual acquisition timestamps remain retained or reversibly available with the modeled records. Aggregation alone does not prove irreversible timestamp disposal.

Collection/aggregation timing is described, but sensor synchronization delays, data-release times and query-time availability checks are not. Recorded future actions are explicitly supplied for conditional forecasting; their use is not automatically an availability violation, but it does not establish an information-availability mechanism.

criteria_met: Variable-length sequences are padded with an accompanying validity mask.
Weekly aggregation distinguishes valid observed days from unavailable days.
Missing zero-imputed final-week sleep is identified for exclusion before coaching simulation.
criteria_missing: The paper does not establish feature-level measured/missing/invalid indicators supplied to the physiological encoder and transition predictor.
Padding validity does not establish that all physiological placeholders are distinguishable from actual measured values.
properties.rationale: Sequence validity treatment is implemented, but comprehensive feature-level missingness conditioning is not demonstrated. The reported sleep exclusions are not generalized into a complete masking mechanism.

Valid-day averaging, weekly indices and recent latent displacement are described, but no per-variable elapsed time since the last genuine observation is specified. The LOCF comparator does not establish measurement-freshness inputs in SensorWM.

Scoped absence concerns the specified transition mechanism: source measurements are placed on a common weekly grid, and equations 33–36 and 50–52 advance state using current latent state, previous displacement and actions, without actual elapsed intervals or native-event timing. Valid-day averaging accommodates incomplete coverage but does not implement irregular-time prediction. This does not assert that source timestamps were discarded.

The paper handles valid observation days, padding and masked decoder targets, but does not specify a model of wear, nonwear, measurement occurrence or acquisition intensity conditional on physiology or context. These masks and aggregation rules alone do not meet the observation-process definition. Explicit assumptions establishing ignorable sampling are also not reported, so absence is not asserted.

Weekly aggregation is motivated as a compromise between variability and sequence length. No target-specific witness-preservation test across aggregated values, update patterns, native timing and external acquisition channels is reported. Downstream classification fidelity and feature correlations do not substitute for that audit.
